body:
Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_4&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Leans on Congress to Address His False Claims of Voter Fraud [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_4&amount=25]
President Trump used his recent State of the Union address and the DHS funding debate to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address his often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. There are stats from the conservative, right-wing Heritage Foundation below that prove it.
The SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE AMERICA ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_4&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE AMERICA Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_4&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=042926_4&amount=35]
How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting. Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Utah recently investigated their entire voter roll of 2.1 million registered voters and found one registered non-citizen who never attempted to vote.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042926_4&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=042926_4&amount=20]

| | | Peter , Our latest fundraising numbers have me so worried that I immediately typed this letter to every single top grassroots conservative we have on file. _The situation is that desperate._ **You see, with the end-of-month deadline rapidly approaching, we're still thousands of dollars **_**SHORT**_** of our goal.** This goal isn't just some arbitrary number that I landed on. We need every last donor to compete with the BILLIONS that Democrats are spending to BUY the midterm elections. **_... Especially now that the Democrats are TIED or AHEAD in the four battleground races that they need to seize control of the Senate and SHATTER the final firewall protecting the President! _** **_New York Times: Why a Democratic Senate, Once Unthinkable, Is a Real Possibility_** **" ...Democrats are ****tied or ahead in ****four**** Republican-held seats****, polls show."** We're already fighting to catch up to the Democrats in the polls, in voter enthusiasm, and most importantly, in voter verifications... The last thing we can afford is to start falling behind in fundraising! As a top America First patriot, I knew I could count on you to read this emergency correspondence. Given all that you've already done for our country, I hate to ask you to do even more, but I have no choice... I'll come right out and say it, ${Recipient.FirstName}: Unlike Democrats (who can count on BILLIONS from Obama's political machine), I don't have any huge checks left to cash or emergency funds left to tap into. At this late hour, dedicated grassroots donors like _YOU_ are my only hope of reaching this goal. You're truly the only place left for me to turn. **But I do want to make one thing clear:** **__[Please only contribute if you’re in the position to do so.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=8426e875f6c94c6b9eb30edb872d4a06&_e=51579hyTmOyzXpxZWIrEVqvVJHauFTrkBmm-ROCi2CYgPdnEDkzdYcQ1A2LN0FMdVaAOfXnVp1DRGiZsFEh6G78t50G19D7QhktExfHns2X0ceHftnYy7a5q0VKfOL46yv8o8UnseZU3Umgjk8iw-VsKR4o6Lm62Uc79UbcY1y7iTgYQw0-KprMPmST2GiOYOZ8MRqYQuO6qEFaqqv8tE6c0HJ1S_-QkJ_y4s1alA8YgfVQJFJ_W0-uOiQDpKpC7MJEe-9FUdH72IttSGh1uX-RIhy09-P_Ud_Ts3UrMCV3NNSZNbQxhCIZ0_aBdNoXWfjyTJEzT7kuJS1lw-SBnvDRUxzh-2MJlZToKpgHofYjhkDj0I-ErjTRMGfndAPgnI_xDkS7Uwfe7Nc60OdOfOZ2yF9a-Chy3F7S4Z-nxrO3KGuAWTRfKxnlUISvf1AHReEJEAs2Abms9Mr8qdaD2vc90TaxHkCB0fAAPbJtvnpyrU0QdGsJXXPQUD-vlpnxxPHK-Uj_0JzTSeJ7YhpkDl-WSg8lgxIVZ3Ut7LyTHlqvbfPNZ4_ZsbvL2FdmhSPOZp76Dlaeuh4FMdFnOuy6QyTlVJVpuePzC7Yf0aDVWjmAHy-yMqNkcVA1oEps7BRB2rkmkxOoU9zmNd7FfxkQJdcLzs7sMY2RLA1KMo0y2m4B1m42o23MXLGIja5_JaL7lulUheM37tAHLyu1tBxit2yOPE6wrPfZ7OBuhfdEOj3U%3D)_ _** Too many fundraising emails these days try to guilt you into donating. name: AOC
subject: We all have to play by the same set of rules.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Democrats in Congress have tried to ban partisan gerrymandering for ten years.
#
_We all have to play by the same set of rules_.
The Republican caucus has made it very clear that they want and are setting rules of partisan gerrymandering.
Democrats in Congress have tried to ban partisan gerrymandering for ten years, but Republicans have rejected it.
We have to all abide by the same rules. If Republicans are going to redraw North Carolina — redraw Texas — if they’re going to redraw and gerrymander every one of their states, then unfortunately we have to provide balance to that until we get to the day where we all can agree to put this behind us and pass a federal ban on partisan gerrymandering.
Our main project now is to **unite the working class in this country against a fascist agenda**. Together, we have to fight against Republican partisan gerrymandering to protect our democracy.

Folks,

I pressed Pete Hegseth on the record about the rampant corruption and conflicts of interest at the Pentagon.

One of the Defense Secretary’s top advisors serves at the Pentagon, but also still maintains a private law practice. Hegseth says he doesn’t know if his advisor represents foreign governments. That is a massive national security concern.

Even though he tried, I refused to let Hegseth dodge my questions. As a three-time combat veteran, I will never shy away from demanding real transparency for our servicemembers and American taxpayers.

When my line of questioning exposed potential conflicts of interest and corruption under his failed leadership, Hegseth got combative. His responses only underscore the importance of demanding real oversight and accountability.

We need to clean up corruption in Washington. The American people deserve a government that works for them, not special interests, foreign governments, or self-enrichment.

Four new House seats are in play after Virginia’s redistricting win. The majority has never been closer — but I need your help to get us there.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260429-2&t=1&akid=3422%2E587540%2EpvZToh)
Peter,
Last week, Virginia voters did something remarkable.
By roughly a 3 point margin, they approved a redistricting referendum that put _four new House seats_ in play, likely Democratic. That puts us one massive step closer to taking back the majority in November.
**In other words: Virginia voters changed the trajectory of the midterms entirely.**
And within 24 hours, a Republican-appointed judge tried to throw out every single one of those votes. They’re scared -- because they know _exactly_ what those four seats mean for their grip on power.
This is the moment we’ve been building towards, Peter. The majority is in reach. And the candidates we push over the finish line between now and November could be the difference between taking back the House and having to watch Trump continue to rip our democracy to shreds without a single check on his power.
That’s what Leaders We Deserve is fighting for. Bold, fearless, people-powered progressives who will offer their constituents a real vision for the future built on transparency, moral courage, and an unwavering commitment to fighting for working people.
But this work isn’t possible without you. We don’t take a dime from corporate PACs or special interests. Every ounce of strength we have to fight for candidates who can take our Party in a direction we can be proud of comes from grassroots supporters like you.
**[Can I count on you to pitch in $5 today to help Leaders We Deserve hit our $50,000 end-of-month fundraising goal so we can keep fighting for the leaders this moment demands?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260429_2_virginia.pjYDhk&refcode=em20260429-3422&amount=5&t=2&akid=3422%2E587540%2EpvZToh)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

| The Trump administration is shamelessly trying to blame Democrats for the rise in political violence in this country.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9768%2E5257348%2Ec3BMAp)
I wish I could say I was surprised, Derek, but the latest attacks against me from the White House are dangerous and yet utterly predictable. This week, Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt **accused me of contributing to the rise of political violence.** Her reasoning? Because I have asserted — all too accurately — that when the president attacks the free press, goes after our universities, weaponizes our justice department, and uses his office to enrich himself and his rich friends, he is using a dictator’s playbook. And he is. But let me be clear: Political violence has no place in our nation, and the attempted attack during the White House Correspondents Dinner is a reminder of how urgently we must act. **But the problem — first and foremost — is coming from inside the White House.** The Trump administration is shamelessly trying to blame Democrats for the rise in political violence in this country. This is the same administration that includes:
* **Kash Patel** , who suggested putting my head on a catapult and shared an AI video of me being buzzsawed.
* **Elon Musk** , who called me a criminal and a traitor — to an audience of millions.
* **Tulsi Gabbard** , who recently accused me of being a “deep state actor” for my work on Donald Trump’s first impeachment.
* **Donald Trump** , who has repeatedly called for my arrest and suggested that veterans serving in Congress should be executed for treason.

This administration is using the White House briefing room to try to intimidate those of us who hold them accountable. **But I am not going anywhere, and I know you aren't either.** The only way to restore sanity to our government is to elect Democratic majorities that will hold this White House accountable. We need to show them that _their tactics of intimidation and blame will not work_. [**Derek, please join me. The inclusion of independent courts in our constitutional design was a stroke of genius for which the founders of our country are widely respected around the world. Beyond serving as forums to resolve private disputes, the courts' fundamental constitutional purpose is to defend rights and democracy writ large from decisions by the political branches that threaten them.
In this context, today's Supreme Court decision didn't just hamstring one of the last major pieces of federal legislation to win a commanding bipartisan majority. It unwound decades of U.S. history, threatening to revive critical parts of Jim Crow and end the era of minority representation in the South.
As the U.S. Supreme Court has grown captured over the past generation by Justices who misled policymakers during their confirmation hearings, however, it has grown weaponized against the very values it was created to defend. Democracy, in particular, has taken a beating at the hands of the Supreme Court--including in a decision issued today that effectively destroyed what little of the Voting Rights Act survived its earlier assaults.

### **Ethical violations undermined the Supreme Court 's legitimacy a long time ago**
Over a decade ago, I wrote a [series](https://substack.com/redirect/0f3bf8ae-693a-4933-a06e-9133dceceb31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of articles published on Huffington Post exploring a crisis in judicial legitimacy.
> Parts I (_[The Politicization of Voting Rights](https://substack.com/redirect/ad9f5a8b-c799-4a64-8e6a-da74989377f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_) and II (_[The Triumph of Politics Over Law](https://substack.com/redirect/15ead550-e770-4f3f-b84c-d0cca9fc77a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_) of this series demonstrated how the Supreme Court, under the leadership of Chief Justice John Roberts, has usurped what once passed for law in pursuit of a conservative political agenda....[T]he Court's conservative majority has "systematically contravened statutory goals, misconstrued statutory terms, [twisted or ignored congressional intent](https://substack.com/redirect/56ab9c26-c36b-46b7-86f5-21039199ef16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and shown disrespect for democratic decision making by legislatures at all levels..."
> Part III (_[Souter's Resignation as an Invitation to Balance a Politicized Court](https://substack.com/redirect/65a17c29-335d-4e49-ae31-f7d21c070b34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_) examined President Obama's first nomination in the context of this historical politicization and suggested potential nominees whose vision and assertiveness could help counter the Court's conservative majority....
> [[Part IV](https://substack.com/redirect/0f3bf8ae-693a-4933-a06e-9133dceceb31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)] examines the _process_ of recent appointments to the Court in the context of the Court's politicized jurisprudence. It explores various ethical violations committed by several sitting conservative Justices: Kennedy, Scalia and Thomas contrived the Court's future nine years ago; Roberts and Scalia have decided cases despite direct conflicts of interest; and Roberts and Alito committed structural violations by intentionally misleading the Senate when seeking confirmation. These examples of inter-branch collusion with Executive officials violate not only the separation of powers doctrine, but also antitrust principles routinely applied to economic markets.
> Concluding its examination, this article challenges the legitimacy of the Court's current composition and suggests how to restore the institution as a guardian of neutral legal principles, immune from politicization or violations of its process....a new structural check on the Court to prevent its future politicization. Specifically, Congress should enact legislation to set 18-year terms for service in the Article III Judiciary. This approach would prevent the Court from being co-opted, ensure regularity in appointments, and preserve the Justices' insulation from political pressures.
Six years ago, while running for Congress, I updated that analysis to succinctly [present](https://substack.com/redirect/38d249de-eb47-44ab-a56b-a274d6885525?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the case for ending life tenure for Supreme Court Justices. I was grateful to see voices including Harvard Law professor Laurence Tribe share that recommendation, and for the Biden administration's eventual [adoption](https://substack.com/redirect/69aac6d8-08f3-4485-8b48-d74ed3ba3c60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of it.

### **The Roberts Court has made a habit of eroded voting rights**
Two years ago, I wrote another article prompted by ensuing court decisions, including the Supreme Court's 2013 decision in _[Shelby County v. Holder](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe479b8-fc7a-47c9-be6d-d029cd325006?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , and the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals' 2022 decision in _[NAACP v. Arkansas Board of Apportionment](https://substack.com/redirect/56f378d4-0826-4fc3-9146-d8d221a6626c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.
Shelby County struck down the preclearance provisions of the Voting Rights Act (VRA) that had granted the federal Department of Justice the power to block proposed changes in voting rights from going into effect until after the proponents had established that their changes would not erode voting rights for racial and ethnic minorities. As I [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/d3c972c1-d18e-41f0-a033-64c6af8b2842?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2024:
> While the Roberts Court's decision in _[Shelby County v. Holder](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe479b8-fc7a-47c9-be6d-d029cd325006?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ (2013)](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe479b8-fc7a-47c9-be6d-d029cd325006?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) did not formally strike down Section 5, it rendered it unenforceable by striking down the coverage formula in Section 4(b). The Court imagined that racial discrimination in the South was a thing of the past, but by hamstringing the VRA's pre-clearance provisions, the Justices effectively invited its escalation. Congress could theoretically muster a majority to update the coverage formula, as the Court suggested in _Shelby County_ , but that's not likely to happen anytime soon given the partisan rancor that prevents Members from agreeing on much beyond [bipartisan weapons sales](https://substack.com/redirect/92aaf44f-de03-43d4-b6d7-dea7f056f553?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
> When the Supreme Court rendered Section 5 effectively unenforceable, some observers suggested that the VRA still had teeth because Section 2 survived. Section 2 is a parallel section allowing private parties to enforce the law after the fact....
The _[NAACP v. Arkansas Board of Apportionment](https://substack.com/redirect/56f378d4-0826-4fc3-9146-d8d221a6626c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ decision--limited to the Eighth Circuit, which hears appeals from federal district courts in Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, and South Dakota--effectively blocked private parties from enforcing Section 2.
Today's decision by the Supreme Court in _[Callais v. Louisiana](https://substack.com/redirect/8ca40f09-672e-49d4-ac18-1dee0ca90e49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ effectively finished the job, by ruling that Section 2 prohibits partisan gerrymanders only when plaintiffs can supply proof of intentional discrimination by state legislatures when drawing districts. Congress never included that limit in the law, which it [reauthorized](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc0661b-ffb1-4634-b985-10f0119cec49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2006 by a _unanimous_ vote in the Senate following a 390-33 vote in the House.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8f416fd2-65d0-4cae-a4b0-e5d69f7c067f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Justice Elena Kagan, joined in dissent by Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, described today's ruling as the "latest chapter in the majority's now-completed demolition of the Voting Rights Act." They wrote:
> The Voting Rights Act is--or, now more accurately, was--'one of the most consequential, efficacious, and amply justified exercises of federal legislative power in our Nation's history.' It was born of the literal blood of Union soldiers and civil rights marchers. It ushered in awe-inspiring change, bringing this Nation closer to fulfilling the ideals of democracy and racial equality. And it has been repeatedly, and overwhelmingly, reauthorized by the people's representatives in Congress....
> States may now draw district lines in ways that undercut the political power of minority voters with virtually no limit.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=195940327&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1OTQwMzI3LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc1MTA2MTAsImV4cCI6MTc4MDEwMjYxMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kpeg0WaN5SvRX7KSNhhgDXznbQ2NGvXbT3dIN7nJhSY)
### **The judicial ethics crisis is even worse than I thought**
I wrote [yesterday](https://substack.com/@shahidbuttar/note/c-250642817?r=97w99) that "[t]here can be no legitimacy to our legal system as long as the most powerful judges in the country can get away with misrepresenting their sources of income, and failing to recuse themselves when parties who fill their pockets appear before their courts.
I have a great many concerns about any number of vectors for corruption, but this might be the most obvious and overt among them."
What prompted my reflection was a recent [article](https://substack.com/redirect/e33159cb-d642-4189-957c-e37eed1ca99a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) originally published on this platform by writer Christopher Armitage. Armitage discovered that:
> Over sixteen years of federal financial disclosure forms, Chief Justice John Roberts mischaracterized more than twenty million dollars in household income from law firms appearing before the Supreme Court. He concealed his wife's equity stake in her employer for three consecutive years. He failed to recuse from more than five hundred cases argued at the Supreme Court by law firms that had paid his household millions in commissions. He architected the Court's first ethics code and designed it to be unenforceable. This is a course of conduct stretching across two decades, connected by a single through-line: the belief that the rules that apply to every other federal judge do not apply to him.
### **The civil rights movement was never victorious, but it was defeated outright today**
Nine years ago, I published [Elusive Victories: Voting Rights, Desegregation and the Erosion of Civil Rights](https://substack.com/redirect/babc7d33-f3b0-456e-9b10-81d9777c8d7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Truthout. The article explored the misunderstood history of the civil rights movement, which has been falsely heralded as victorious even though it "was denied its most visionary goals by a policy establishment unwilling to grant them." As I explained then:
> Civil rights leaders had hoped to secure a right to employment, food, housing, education and health care--all of which were goals that [Dr. King](https://substack.com/redirect/89b7cdb7-0573-4d26-b29d-ebaad85fbebc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) explicitly referenced. Among its various goals, desegregation and voting rights were the only two ultimately secured in law and policy.
In this context, today's Supreme Court decision didn't just hamstring one of the last major pieces of federal legislation to win a commanding bipartisan majority. It unwound decades of U.S. history, threatening to revive critical parts of Jim Crow and end the era of minority representation in the South.

Meanwhile, further | | | Apr 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | The inclusion of independent courts in our constitutional design was a stroke of genius for which the founders of our country are widely respected around the world. Beyond serving as forums to resolve private disputes, the courts' fundamental constitutional purpose is to defend rights and democracy writ large from decisions by the political branches that threaten them. In this context, today's Supreme Court decision didn't just hamstring one of the last major pieces of federal legislation to win a commanding bipartisan majority. It unwound decades of U.S. history, threatening to revive critical parts of Jim Crow and end the era of minority representation in the South. As the U.S. Supreme Court has grown captured over the past generation by Justices who misled policymakers during their confirmation hearings, however, it has grown weaponized against the very values it was created to defend. Democracy, in particular, has taken a beating at the hands of the Supreme Court--including in a decision issued today that effectively destroyed what little of the Voting Rights Act survived its earlier assaults. Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! Help inform your friends by sharing this post. Ethical violations undermined the Supreme Court 's legitimacy a long time ago Over a decade ago, I wrote a of articles published on Huffington Post exploring a crisis in judicial legitimacy. Part III () examined President Obama's first nomination in the context of this historical politicization and suggested potential nominees whose vision and assertiveness could help counter the Court's conservative majority.... ] examines the process of recent appointments to the Court in the context of the Court's politicized jurisprudence. These examples of inter-branch collusion with Executive officials violate not only the separation of powers doctrine, but also antitrust principles routinely applied to economic markets. Concluding its examination, this article challenges the legitimacy of the Court's current composition and suggests how to restore the institution as a guardian of neutral legal principles, immune from politicization or violations of its process....a new structural check on the Court to prevent its future politicization. Specifically, Congress should enact legislation to set 18-year terms for service in the Article III Judiciary. This approach would prevent the Court from being co-opted, ensure regularity in appointments, and preserve the Justices' insulation from political pressures. **" Corpus Christi delays action on plan to cut water use by 25% if emergency is declared"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/e65116a3-9c2d-4896-9bde-b30cddcb1272?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Colleen DeGuzman** - The Corpus Christi City Council unanimously agreed Tuesday to delay a vote on how much residents, local businesses and refineries would have to cut water if a supply crisis is triggered.

**Nick Winkelmann** , chief operating officer of the city's water department, presented a plan to require all customers of the city's water system to reduce use by 25% during a Level 1 emergency -- the point when the water supply is projected to be 180 days from falling short of demand. Experts say that may happen as soon as September unless significant rain falls.

Council members told Winkelmann they needed more information on how curtailment would be enforced -- including fines and fees for customers who violate limits -- before settling on a rate.

"It's very difficult to vote on something where you don't know the end result," Council Member **Gil Hernandez** said. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/e65116a3-9c2d-4896-9bde-b30cddcb1272?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" 10 current and former Mexican officials accused in US indictment of aiding drug trafficking"** via AP**** - The governor of Sinaloa and nine other current and former Mexican officials were charged with drug trafficking and weapons offenses in a U.S. indictment unsealed Wednesday in New York, accused of aiding in the massive importation of illicit narcotics into the United States.

Some officials were members of Mexico's progressive ruling party, Morena, posing a political conundrum for [Mexican President ](https://substack.com/redirect/22e6435e-41bc-4e7b-b502-cfcb39f31e15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Claudia Sheinbaum](https://substack.com/redirect/22e6435e-41bc-4e7b-b502-cfcb39f31e15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as [she seeks to offset mounting pressures](https://substack.com/redirect/dad2aa58-e7e5-477a-a81d-22eeea90b3f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Trump administration. Some of those politicians called the indictment a political attack on their party.

U.S. federal officials announced the charges in a news release. None of the defendants were in custody, but Mexico's government said shortly afterward that it had received multiple extradition requests from the U.S. without identifying those requested. It did not say how it would respond.

The 10 people charged in Manhattan federal court are current and former government or law enforcement officials in Sinaloa, including **Rub en Rocha Moya**, 76, who has been governor of Mexico's Sinaloa state since November 2021.

Charges against Moya included narcotics importation conspiracy and possession of machine guns and destructive devices, along with another conspiracy count. If convicted, he could face life in prison or a mandatory minimum of 40 years behind bars. (_[AP](https://substack.com/redirect/4b15a568-9d70-49a9-8873-158154474189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Texas earns 22nd 'best state for business' title as GDP hits $2.9T"** via [InnovationMap](https://substack.com/redirect/33a77a54-bbb8-4652-84ee-3e04ee662fb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **John Egan** - The Texas business sector recently received a double dose of good news. For the 22nd consecutive year, Chief Executive magazine named Texas the best state for business. In tandem with that achievement, preliminary new estimates from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis show the size of Texas' economy jumped to $2.9 trillion in 2025, up by a nation-leading growth rate of 2.5 percent compared with the previous year.

Speaking about the Chief Executive honor, Gov. **Greg Abbott** says Texas benefits from pro-growth policies, a strong workforce, strategic investments in education, training for high-demand skills and the presence of critical infrastructure.

"Texas is where businesses innovate and where opportunity abounds. ... We will continue to move at the speed of business as we build a more prosperous Texas for generations to come," the governor says.

An annual Chief Executive survey of CEOs, presidents and business owners determines which state is the best for business. Texas has landed at No. 1 every year since Chief Executive launched the ranking. _([InnovationMap](https://substack.com/redirect/33a77a54-bbb8-4652-84ee-3e04ee662fb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Disaster declarations ripple through South Texas amid water crisis"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/90db58ff-5409-4d4f-aa5d-bbaec24b115c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - At least six small cities and towns in the Coastal Bend region of Texas issued disaster declarations in the last two weeks, begging not to be forgotten amid a spiraling water crisis.

All attention lies on the city of Corpus Christi as it grapples with the growing likelihood of an unprecedented disaster. But Corpus Christi, the eighth-largest city in Texas, doesn't just provide water to its own industries and residents. It supplies the entire seven-county region, including 20 other municipalities.

"Everyone is like, 'What the heck is going on and what do we do?" said **Elida Castillo** , mayor of the small town of Taft, which issued a disaster declaration on April 21. "I'm just trying to figure out what we could do."

**Editorial: "Ken Paxton's penchant for frivolous lawsuits"** via Dallas Morning News - Attorney General **Ken Paxton 's** office has been spewing out lawsuits and investigations faster than a pitching machine set to high. We think we know why: Each new action typically produces free media attention while he's in the final stretch of a vicious primary runoff for a U.S. Senate seat.

In recent weeks, his office has announced moves against music streaming services, California-based kratom retailers and the online Democratic fundraising platform ActBlue. He's gone after makers of yoga pants, televisions and some Texas cities and universities. Last year, two toothpaste companies were among his targets.

Paxton hasn't sued a ham sandwich -- yet -- but don't bet against it.

There are many problems with Paxton's leadership as attorney general, but his profligacy with lawsuits and investigations is a particular concern. Their sheer volume makes it hard to know which confront important issues, and which were dreamed up to appeal to plaintiff's attorneys or the State Republican Executive Committee.

The Attorney General's office has serious responsibilities, such as enforcing child support laws and deciding how much information local and state government agencies can withhold from the public. And Paxton's office has brought or joined important cases, including ones against Meta and TikTok, focused on protecting privacy and minors. But any good work the AG does is buried under mountains of frivolous, harmful or purely partisan acts.

The toothpaste investigation wasted public resources. The AG's office claimed that makers of fluoride toothpaste jeopardized consumer safety by using "misleading, deceptive, and dangerous" marketing.

The AG argued that fluoride is harmful -- and high doses can be -- so packaging that shows a thick swirl of toothpaste on a tot's toothbrush causes parents to poison their children. Moms and dads may put too much paste on their child's toothbrush, but the best place to address that concern is a pediatrician's office, not a courtroom.

The case against the makers of Tylenol and other acetaminophen products was more fraught. Paxton, echoing President Donald Trump, falsely claimed that taking the drug during pregnancy can cause autism in a fetus. Repeated research, including a study published online this month, has shown that appropriate use of the medication during pregnancy is not linked to a higher risk of autism.

The AG won a temporary restraining order against the manufacturers, not because the drug causes autism, but because they failed to file and maintain their state business registrations. Meanwhile, the lawsuit about paperwork problems promoted medical misinformation. That's harmful.

Making the situation even more shameful, Paxton's well-staffed office brought in private attorneys, whose fees usually exceed the cost of using in-house lawyers, to help pursue the case.

Texas legislators, with Republicans usually leading the charge, reformed state tort laws to quash frivolous lawsuits and improve our business climate. It should be disturbing to GOP lawmakers to watch one of their own so often misuse the civil legal system. It certainly disturbs us. (_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/45345bb8-a7d0-41de-bc6c-ea771307feed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

While no major new sales tax legislation was passed in the most recent session, the foundational law called House Bill 1223 (HB 1223), passed in 2013 during the 83rd Legislature and signed by then-Gov. **Rick Perry** , continues to drive investment.

HB 1223 created Texas Tax Code §151.359, establishing a temporary state sales and use tax exemption for qualifying data centers. Subsequent amendments have expanded the program, which remains active today.

Texas is continuing to lead the nation in the number of businesses filing bankruptcy, new data show, with one of every six U.S. cases being filed in the state.

The Texas business bankruptcy boom comes as the number of filings across the nation is topping pre-pandemic levels, an extension of a trend that began in 2022.

Texas pride runs deep, right down to Lone Star residents' wallet.

It's no secret that Texans love to support local, homegrown brands, but a new study released this week outlines which Texas-founded companies have garnered the most trust and consumer rapport in the Lone Star State.

LSG -- a communications and public affairs organization based in Washington, D.C. with a Texas outpost in The Woodlands -- surveyed 1,500 people across Austin, Dallas and Houston earlier this year to gauge which brands they trust the most, releasing the findings on Thursday, April 23. Among those surveyed, 86% of respondents said they "strongly identify with Texas culture and identity" and utilize that via their purchasing habits.

The brands that earned the most respect and support? **H-E-B** , **Whataburger** , **Buc-ee 's**, **Blue Bell** and **Dr Pepper** led the Texas masses in garnering the most substantial customer buy-in, LSG's analysis revealed. _([MySA](https://substack.com/redirect/5430b6f3-0d29-44cd-98d7-934478008cbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

TOP NEWS " Corpus Christi delays action on plan to cut water use by 25% if emergency is declared" via Colleen DeGuzman - The Corpus Christi City Council unanimously agreed Tuesday to delay a vote on how much residents, local businesses and refineries would have to cut water if a supply crisis is triggered. Nick Winkelmann , chief operating officer of the city's water department, presented a plan to require all customers of the city's water system to reduce use by 25% during a Level 1 emergency -- the point when the water supply is projected to be 180 days from falling short of demand. Experts say that may happen as soon as September unless significant rain falls. Council members told Winkelmann they needed more information on how curtailment would be enforced -- including fines and fees for customers who violate limits -- before settling on a rate. "It's very difficult to vote on something where you don't know the end result," Council Member Gil Hernandez said. () " 10 current and former Mexican officials accused in US indictment of aiding drug trafficking" via AP - The governor of Sinaloa and nine other current and former Mexican officials were charged with drug trafficking and weapons offenses in a U.S. indictment unsealed Wednesday in New York, accused of aiding in the massive importation of illicit narcotics into the United States. Some officials were members of Mexico's progressive ruling party, Morena, posing a political conundrum for as from the Trump administration. Some of those politicians called the indictment a political attack on their party. U.S. federal officials announced the charges in a news release. None of the defendants were in custody, but Mexico's government said shortly afterward that it had received multiple extradition requests from the U.S. without identifying those requested. It did not say how it would respond. The 10 people charged in Manhattan federal court are current and former government or law enforcement officials in Sinaloa, including Rub en Rocha Moya, 76, who has been governor of Mexico's Sinaloa state since November 2021. Charges against Moya included narcotics importation conspiracy and possession of machine guns and destructive devices, along with another conspiracy count. If convicted, he could face life in prison or a mandatory minimum of 40 years behind bars. () " Texas earns 22nd 'best state for business' title as GDP hits $2.9T" via John Egan - The Texas business sector recently received a double dose of good news. For the 22nd consecutive year, Chief Executive magazine named Texas the best state for business. In tandem with that achievement, preliminary new estimates from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis show the size of Texas' economy jumped to $2.9 trillion in 2025, up by a nation-leading growth rate of 2.5 percent compared with the previous year. Speaking about the Chief Executive honor, Gov. Greg Abbott says Texas benefits from pro-growth policies, a strong workforce, strategic investments in education, training for high-demand skills and the presence of critical infrastructure. "Texas is where businesses innovate and where opportunity abounds. ... We will continue to move at the speed of business as we build a more prosperous Texas for generations to come," the governor says. An annual Chief Executive survey of CEOs, presidents and business owners determines which state is the best for business. Texas has landed at No. 1 every year since Chief Executive launched the ranking. () " Disaster declarations ripple through South Texas amid water crisis" via - At least six small cities and towns in the Coastal Bend region of Texas issued disaster declarations in the last two weeks, begging not to be forgotten amid a spiraling water crisis. All attention lies on the city of Corpus Christi as it grapples with the growing likelihood of an unprecedented disaster. But Corpus Christi, the eighth-largest city in Texas, doesn't just provide water to its own industries and residents. It supplies the entire seven-county region, including 20 other municipalities. "Everyone is like, 'What the heck is going on and what do we do?" said Elida Castillo , mayor of the small town of Taft, which issued a disaster declaration on April 21. "I'm just trying to figure out what we could do." Castillo recently organized a town hall meeting on the water crisis for the 3,000 residents of Taft, but officials from Corpus Christi didn't show up. She hasn't heard much from county or state officials either. She is getting a sense that nobody knows what to do, and she isn't alone. () " North Texas tornadoes kill two as storms slam Wise and Parker counties" via Kelley - Two people were killed when powerful tornadoes ripped through Wise and Parker counties late Saturday night, April 25. National Weather Service survey teams confirmed Sunday that an EF-2 tornado with peak winds of 135 mph struck the Runaway Bay area in Wise County, killing one person and injuring at least six others while causing major structural damage and displacing about 20 families. In Parker County, an EF-1 tornado with winds up to 105 mph hit near Springtown, where a second victim died after a mobile home collapsed south of town. Wise County Judge J.D. Clark said emergency responders from across North Texas worked through the night clearing debris and helping residents reach damaged homes. Officials reported widespread power outages and significant destruction in neighborhoods along Cumberland Trail and Overland Trail in Runaway Bay. Parker County Emergency Services also responded to reports of structural collapses and injuries. The deadly storms were part of a slow-moving severe weather system that prompted multiple tornado warnings across the region around 9 p.m. Saturday. No additional fatalities have been reported () " Texas State's active shooter training facility set for $25M expansion" via Molly Wilhelm - A multimillion-dollar upgrade is planned for TSU's ALERRT Center, focused on active shooter response training. Texas State University's active shooter training hub could soon get a multimillion-dollar upgrade. An $18.75 million expansion is planned for the Advanced Law Enforcement Rapid Response Training (ALERRT) Center at TSU, according to a recent filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Registration. While details submitted to the TDLR are subject to change, construction could break ground this month and last approximately a year. A new 31,300-square-foot building, with a 16,480-square-foot warehouse and a two-story, 14,820-square-foot administrative suite, is planned for the 1285 William Pettus Rd. site in San Marcos. Associated mechanical, electrical, plumbing, parking, driveways and loading docks are also among details. () " Businesses prepare as World Cup crowds expected to flood North Texas" via Spillyards - Businesses across North Texas are preparing for an estimated 4 million visitors expected during the World Cup. Owners say they are expanding inventory and planning for demand, though the scale of the event brings uncertainty. With just over a month until the World Cup arrives in North Texas, local businesses are preparing for an expected surge of visitors and spending tied to the global event. Projections show the region could host about 4 million people for nine matches, more than any other host city, with billions of dollars expected to flow into the economy. At Whiski Designs in the Dallas Farmers Market, World Cup merchandise is already filling shelves. () 2026 Editorial: "Ken Paxton's penchant for frivolous lawsuits" via Dallas Morning News - Attorney General Ken Paxton 's office has been spewing out lawsuits and investigations faster than a pitching machine set to high. We think we know why: Each new action typically produces free media attention while he's in the final stretch of a vicious primary runoff for a U.S. Senate seat. In recent weeks, his office has announced moves against music streaming services, California-based kratom retailers and the online Democratic fundraising platform ActBlue. He's gone after makers of yoga pants, televisions and some Texas cities and universities. Last year, two toothpaste companies were among his targets. Paxton hasn't sued a ham sandwich -- yet -- but don't bet against it. There are many problems with Paxton's leadership as attorney general, but his profligacy with lawsuits and investigations is a particular concern. Their sheer volume makes it hard to know which confront important issues, and which were dreamed up to appeal to plaintiff's attorneys or the State Republican Executive Committee. The Attorney General's office has serious responsibilities, such as enforcing child support laws and deciding how much information local and state government agencies can withhold from the public. And Paxton's office has brought or joined important cases, including ones against Meta and TikTok, focused on protecting privacy and minors. But any good work the AG does is buried under mountains of frivolous, harmful or purely partisan acts. The toothpaste investigation wasted public resources. The AG's office claimed that makers of fluoride toothpaste jeopardized consumer safety by using "misleading, deceptive, and dangerous" marketing. The AG argued that fluoride is harmful -- and high doses can be -- so packaging that shows a thick swirl of toothpaste on a tot's toothbrush causes parents to poison their children. Moms and dads may put too much paste on their child's toothbrush, but the best place to address that concern is a pediatrician's office, not a courtroom. The case against the makers of Tylenol and other acetaminophen products was more fraught. Paxton, echoing President Donald Trump, falsely claimed that taking the drug during pregnancy can cause autism in a fetus. Repeated research, including a study published online this month, has shown that appropriate use of the medication during pregnancy is not linked to a higher risk of autism. The AG won a temporary restraining order against the manufacturers, not because the drug causes autism, but because they failed to file and maintain their state business registrations. Meanwhile, the lawsuit about paperwork problems promoted medical misinformation. That's harmful. Making the situation even more shameful, Paxton's well-staffed office brought in private attorneys, whose fees usually exceed the cost of using in-house lawyers, to help pursue the case. Texas legislators, with Republicans usually leading the charge, reformed state tort laws to quash frivolous lawsuits and improve our business climate. It should be disturbing to GOP lawmakers to watch one of their own so often misuse the civil legal system. It certainly disturbs us. () " It's official: SCOTUS says Texas' GOP-friendly congressional maps can stay" via Andrea Drusch - New Texas congressional maps drawn to give Republicans an advantage in the 2026 midterm election are here to stay, the Supreme Court ruled Monday. Texas lawmakers approved the maps at President Donald Trump 's request last summer, and candidates quickly started lining up for races based on those new boundaries. Though Democrats have long insisted GOP leaders broke the law by packing minority voters into a smaller number of districts, their brief victory in a federal court last November was quickly reversed by a temporary Supreme Court order aimed at providing candidates clarity during the filing period to run for office. Since then, the new maps have been treated as law of the land, and got the official seal of approval from a conservative-dominated Supreme Court on Monday. () " Texas Railroad Commission GOP runoff: Who is running and what to know" via Nogueras Ramos and Mar ia Mendez - The Railroad Commission, one of Texas' oldest regulatory agencies, oversees a constellation of energy infrastructure across the state. Its elected commissioners and staff are tasked with regulating oil and gas production, natural gas facilities, hydrogen, pipelines, coal and uranium surface mining. The agency has not regulated railroads since 2005. With several field offices across Texas, the commission inspects facilities, enforces penalties and reports to the Texas Legislature. More recently, the agency has also taken on regulating hydrogen storage and carbon dioxide injection and storage, as companies look to create alternate sources of energy and take advantage of federal financial incentives to recapture carbon dioxide that contributes to climate change. Far and away, Texas commands the U.S. oil and gas trade. The industry drills more oil and other hydrocarbons than all the other states combined. This massive industry employs nearly half a million Texans and pays billions of dollars in taxes to local and state coffers. And it's changing. Seeking to become more profitable, oil companies are evolving their business models to expand their ability to deliver natural gas -- which powers electricity generation -- to data centers. Oil companies are also set to build facilities designed to inject carbon dioxide underground to reduce air pollution. The commission will oversee and regulate these ventures. Additionally, as Texas becomes more prone to extreme weather, the agency is responsible for ensuring that natural gas facilities are prepared to avoid shortages or incidents that could affect the state's power grid and lead to widespread power outages. In the GOP runoff, incumbent Railroad Commissioner Jim Wright is pitching himself as a "proven advocate for Texas energy" who also values "high environmental and safety standards." Meanwhile, challenger Bo French has cast himself as a "MAGA conservative" who wants "to give Trump the backing he needs" in the energy industry. Carlos Nogueras Ramos is a regional reporter based in Odessa. Carlos joined The Texas Tribune in 2023 as a corps member with Report for America. Carlos tells the stories of Texas from the vast energy-rich regions of the state. Mar ia Mendez works on efforts to better connect with Texans and writes explainers and guides. She strives to answer Texans' questions about politics and public policy and to help them find resources. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Texas regulators aren't keeping up with data centers" via Kathryn Guerra - Artificial intelligence data center development is rapidly expanding in Texas, but so too are concerns about whether the state's environmental agency, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, can effectively regulate the industry. Texas will soon lead the nation in the number of data centers, with Dallas-Fort Worth as the epicenter of resource-intensive operations. State leaders, including Gov. Greg Abbott , are touting the economic benefit of massive AI data centers, while handing over billions in tax breaks to tech industry giants in recent years. If you're one of the many Texans concerned about Big Tech's rapid expansion, the TCEQ's most recent performance metrics may give you reason to wonder if it is up to the job. TCEQ issues the permits that AI data centers need to operate gas-powered turbines and diesel generators and to discharge wastewater from cooling operations. Issuing permits isn't a problem for the state regulator, which handed out 9,000 new permits last year, according to the agency's own reporting. But one of TCEQ's primary functions - and struggles - is conducting on-site compliance inspections. ) " Texas teachers can make money off school vouchers. Here's how." via Xochilt Garcia - School choice advocates seeking to get the word out about Texas Education Freedom Accounts are now working to educate educators on how the program can open opportunities for teachers to earn money outside of their day jobs. TEFAs are voucher-like awards that families can use to pay for private school tuition and for education services like tutoring, therapy, curriculum, specialists and more. "There's a lot of opportunity," said Zoe Alterman , speaking to a group of educators from across San Antonio during a teacher happy hour at Vibras on April 16. "It's a very, very wide range of what is considered educational products." Alterman, a master social worker who's worked as a teacher, nonprofit leader and tutor, is working with the School Discovery Network to guide teachers and educators through the vendor application process for the voucher program. () " Gov. Abbott honors 25 fallen officers at Texas Peace Officers Memorial Ceremony in Austin" via Marco Bitonel - Hundreds gathered at the Texas Capitol to honor fallen officers as 25 names were added to the state memorial. The roar of bagpipes could be heard Sunday afternoon, as hundreds of police officers made their way from Congress Avenue to the Texas Capitol building. The procession was a part of the Texas Peace Officers' Memorial Ceremony, recognizing those who have given their lives in the line of duty. In total, 25 new names were engraved onto the memorial monument, honoring peace officers who had died in 2025 as well as those who died in the line of duty in previous years. () #TXLEGE " Texas revives push to overhaul flood safety requirements" via - Texas lawmakers plan to revisit legislation to improve emergency preparedness in the wake of last summer's deadly floods -- and they may try to prevent a summer camp at the center of the tragedy from reopening. State legislative committees investigating the July 2025 disaster wrapped up a two-day hearing Tuesday, setting the table for a major policy debate that will spill into next year. About 135 people died from the catastrophic floods over the July 4th weekend, including 119 in Kerr County along the Guadalupe River. Twenty-seven of the deaths occurred at Camp Mystic, a family-run summer camp for girls located on the river in south-central Texas. The Texas Legislature passed bills during a special session last year that standardized training and staffing levels for summer camps and forbids the state from licensing camps that have cabins within 1,000 feet of floodways. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Austin approved $1B in projects. Many still aren't built." via Chaya Tong - The Mexic-Arte Museum on Congress Avenue in Austin has spent two decades awaiting renovations to its deteriorating, city-owned building, delayed in part by insufficient bond funding. The structure dates to 1910. For more than a decade, the intersection near Priscilla Glover 's Zilker home has been a hazard. As the neighborhood has grown, more drivers run the four-way stop. Glover has grown used to the sound of T-bone collisions -- tires screeching, then an unmistakable crunch. "We're desperate for a turning signal," she said. "It's just not safe." In 2016, it seemed relief was coming. That November, Austin voters approved a $720 million bond to improve safety and transportation in neighborhoods including those along South Lamar Boulevard, which would add a traffic light at Glover's intersection. Ten years later, the light still isn't there. Neither are many of the other upgrades included in the South Lamar Corridor Project, which is one small piece of a much larger problem. () Editorial: "Dallas City Hall can't keep spending, but will council do what's necessary?" via Dallas Morning News - Dallas City Manager Kimberly Bizor Tolbert i s willing to face budget reality, even if the City Council is not. Tolbert's announcement Friday that she is taking steps to slow spending at City Hall amid falling revenues and growing costs is more than welcome. We just wish the council would show the same willingness to tighten up. Tolbert sent a memo to her department directors Friday morning that detailed what we read as a $34 million budget gap that has opened this fiscal year. We aren't surprised. The price of paying cops and firefighters and adding to their pensions has only grown since voters adopted a referendum requiring the city to increase police hiring and pay. () " Houston mall's demolition could make way for a future high-speed train" via Peter Warren - Crews have begun the process of demolishing the old Northwest Mall with the hope that the location near the 610 Loop and U.S. 290 will one day become a train station, according to a developer. Texas High Speed Rail Holdings LLC, previously known as Texas Central, is attempting to build a high-speed train between Dallas and Houston. The company aims to build its Houston terminal on the mall property if its plans for the high-speed rail get approved. Demolition is expected to take approximately 12 months. "Removal of the legacy mall and adjacent structures on the 45-acre parcel is another step forward," a Texas High-Speed Rail Holdings spokesperson said in a statement. "This is important early enabling and foundation work that will allow the project to proceed as soon as we get the green light. Once approved, the project will create jobs and help drive important economic growth for Texas." () " Fort Worth ISD leader addresses proposed staff cuts, school closure before vote" via Ruiz - Peter Licata , the state-appointed superintendent of the Fort Worth school district, acknowledged the tough decisions behind potential staff reductions and another school closure that will be voted on at Tuesday's board meeting. In an interview with the Star-Telegram on Monday, April 27, Superintendent Peter Licata addressed the proposed closure of International Newcomer Academy, 5% teacher raises going into effect next school year, and cuts to vacant positions that he says brought $40 million back into the district's budget this year. He described these decisions and proposals, among others, as necessary to drive the district in a positive direction. The flurry of changes to the district came forward after Licata and a nine-person Board of Managers were appointed by Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath to lead the district during a state takeover, which was prompted by the district's years of stagnant academic performance. The Board of Managers approved a reduction in force at its last meeting two weeks ago and is set to vote on another reduction in force on Tuesday, in addition to the proposed closure of International Newcomer Academy. The campus serves refugee and immigrant students in grades 6-9. () " Rising demand push CPS Energy toward more natural gas, testing climate goals" via Kelsey Brown - CPS Energy's updated generation plan would lean more into natural gas and solar power, while cutting reliance on the wholesale market as part of a long-term strategy. Surging demand for power is spurring CPS Energy to revamp its energy generation plan, moving the utility further from its goal for less reliance on fossil fuels. The need to reevaluate the utility's generation plan came after the utility forecast that its capacity under the current plan will fall short of being able to meet demand by the start of the next decade. The gap is driven by the high level of growth locally and across the state, as well as increased costs required to build out new energy generation sources, said David Kee , the utility's director of energy market policy. () " VIA adds $5.2M to its Green Line project now under construction" via Shari Biediger - VIA Metropolitan Transit this week approved another $5.2 million in spending for its multi-million dollar Green Line. The VIA board of trustees gave the green light to modify a contract with Parsons Transportation Group for design services during construction on the $480.8 million project. The Green Line is the north-south transit line of VIA Advanced Rapid Transit project which will create a system of corridors designed to get riders faster to their destination using dedicated bus lanes, prioritized traffic signals and more frequent pickups and dropoffs. Selected via a request for proposals, the Virginia-based Parsons won a five-year design contract in March 2024 for the Green Line worth over $20.8 million plus a 10% contingency fund. In 2025, VIA amended the contract to increase the initial contingency amount, adding another $4.2 million and bringing the contract total to just over $27 million. The latest contract modification to extend design services and increase the contingency brings the contract value to just under $32.3 million. But the project remains under budget, said a VIA spokesman, with the most recent change already having been included in this year's budget. () " Mayor Whitmire faces ethics complaints over city-funded podcast" via Dominic Walsh - After Houston Public Media reported Whitmire's new podcast costs up to $60,000, the Houston Progressive Caucus said it filed ethics complaints with local and state authorities. Mayor John Whitmire is facing formal ethics complaints from the Houston Progressive Caucus over his new podcast, "901 Bagby: Inside the Mayor's Office." According to members of the caucus, the group filed grievances over the past week with the Texas Ethics Commission, the city of Houston's Inspector General, and the City Controller's waste, fraud and abuse division. The complaints came after Houston Public Media obtained documents showing the podcast costs up to $60,000 in public funds. Because the podcast is taxpayer-funded, the group argued Whitmire's brief allusion to next year's municipal election during the first episode of the podcast ran afoul of state ethics rules around political advertising. () " City of Victoria enters into settlement with opioid distributors" via Lindsey Plotkin - The Victoria City Council approved an opioid lawsuit settlement agreement during Tuesday's meeting. Through the Texas Attorney General's Office, the city has been participating since October 2021 in the lawsuit filed against manufacturers for their role in the opioid epidemic. After approval during Tuesday's meeting, the City of Victoria will enter into the sixth round of settlements. It has received $56,927.75 from the previous five settlements. "This resolution would approve the City joining the sixth round of settlement agreements with six Remnant Defendants: Associated Pharmacies, Inc. (and American Associated Pharmacies); J M Smith Corporation; Louisiana Wholesale Drug Company, Inc.; Morris and Dickson Co.; North Carolina Mutual Wholesale Drug Company, Inc.; and United Natural Foods, Inc. (including its subsidiaries SuperValu and Advantage Logistics)," the agenda item memo said. According to the AG's office, the state has received over $3.3 billion in total from Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family, widely referred to as two of the biggest influences of the opioid epidemic. The money has been distributed to participating municipalities. () BUSINESS NEWS " The San Angelo Data Center Will Qualify for a Huge Tax Incentive. Will More Tax Breaks Follow?" via - The Texas Legislature wants the state to remain a national leader in data center development. While no major new sales tax legislation was passed in the most recent session, the foundational law called House Bill 1223 (HB 1223), passed in 2013 during the 83rd Legislature and signed by then-Gov. Rick Perry , continues to drive investment. HB 1223 created Texas Tax Code §151.359, establishing a temporary state sales and use tax exemption for qualifying data centers. Subsequent amendments have expanded the program, which remains active today. The 2013 law exempts the 6.25% state portion of sales and use tax on items "necessary and essential" to the operation of a qualified data center. Eligible purchases include: Local sales taxes, (typically 1.5% city + 0.5% county in San Angelo) are not exempted, only the statewide rate is. To qualify, a data center generally must: () " Business bankruptcies surge in Texas amid economic pressures" via Flahive - Joann Fabrics filed bankruptcy and closed all its stores in 2025 after a failed attempt to find a buyer. Like many retailers, it suffered from declining post-pandemic sales and high debt. Texas is continuing to lead the nation in the number of businesses filing bankruptcy, new data show, with one of every six U.S. cases being filed in the state. The Texas business bankruptcy boom comes as the number of filings across the nation is topping pre-pandemic levels, an extension of a trend that began in 2022. The increases are tied to economic pressures including persistent inflation, the impact of tariffs and rising interest rates and consumer debt. () " These are Texans' most trusted, favorite Lone Star brands" via Kelsey Thompson - Buc-ee's and H-E-B are among Texans' most trusted and favorite homegrown brands, according to an April 2026 survey conducted by Washington, D.C.-based firm LSG. Texas pride runs deep, right down to Lone Star residents' wallet. It's no secret that Texans love to support local, homegrown brands, but a new study released this week outlines which Texas-founded companies have garnered the most trust and consumer rapport in the Lone Star State. LSG -- a communications and public affairs organization based in Washington, D.C. with a Texas outpost in The Woodlands -- surveyed 1,500 people across Austin, Dallas and Houston earlier this year to gauge which brands they trust the most, releasing the findings on Thursday, April 23. Among those surveyed, 86% of respondents said they "strongly identify with Texas culture and identity" and utilize that via their purchasing habits. The brands that earned the most respect and support? H-E-B , Whataburger , Buc-ee 's, Blue Bell and Dr Pepper led the Texas masses in garnering the most substantial customer buy-in, LSG's analysis revealed. Peter,this is a day we’ll remember for the rest of our lives.
This Supreme Court ruling has effectively gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, nullifying critical protections for communities of color.
This is a devastating blow to the crown jewel of the civil rights movement — denigrating the sacrifices that generations of Americans made for every American to have an equal voice in our democracy. This ruling will have seismic effects on the ability of communities of color to be represented in the halls of power.
Let’s make one thing clear: we have been preparing for this ruling. But the same can be said for anti-democracy forces across the country. As you read this, extremist politicians are rapidly drawing up plans to continue to push mid-decade redraws and potentially upend minority opportunity districts across the country.
**Redistricting Action was built for this moment, and we’re ready to fight like hell. Today’s decision made clear that _we are in the middle of the civil rights fight of our generation,_ and it’s a test we simply cannot fail.**

clean_body: We’ve been preparing for this devastating ruling, and we’re ready to fight back. | Peter,this is a day we’ll remember for the rest of our lives. This Supreme Court ruling has effectively gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, nullifying critical protections for communities of color. This is a devastating blow to the crown jewel of the civil rights movement — denigrating the sacrifices that generations of Americans made for every American to have an equal voice in our democracy. This ruling will have seismic effects on the ability of communities of color to be represented in the halls of power. Let’s make one thing clear: we have been preparing for this ruling. But the same can be said for anti-democracy forces across the country. As you read this, extremist politicians are rapidly drawing up plans to continue to push mid-decade redraws and potentially upend minority opportunity districts across the country. Redistricting Action was built for this moment, and we’re ready to fight like hell. Today’s decision made clear that we are in the middle of the civil rights fight of our generation, and it’s a test we simply cannot fail. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = Here’s what happens next: Louisiana’s fair voting map that includes two Black-opportunity districts has been thrown out. Friends, this is dark.
Donald Trump’s Supreme Court strikes devastating blow after devastating blow to our rights and values. Today, it was with a decision that gutted the remaining protections of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 — a law that has been reauthorized multiple times in Congress on a bipartisan basis.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
The VRA has been a cornerstone of our Civil Rights movement — born, as Justice Elena Kagan said in her dissent, “of the literal blood of Union soldiers and civil rights marchers.” To remove its protections is to blatantly open the door for racial discrimination, setting back our country’s ongoing struggle to secure truly equal rights for all.
There’s not an easy answer here. The impacts of SCOTUS decisions can reverberate for generations, and we don’t yet know the full damage of this one. But I can tell you one thing:
Our fight to flip the House and reclaim a Democratic majority so we can put a check on Trump’s power has never been more important.
Justice Kagan also said this of the VRA: “It has been repeatedly, and overwhelmingly, reauthorized by the people’s representatives in Congress. Only they have the right to say it is no longer needed — not the Members of this Court.”
We must continue the fight to end voter suppression and protect voting rights in Congress, and we can only do that with a Democratic majority. Will you contribute any amount towards this work today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]

subject: Chris Rabb’s opponent just dropped out of the debate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
Dr. Ala Stanford is not qualified or prepared to be the leader Philadelphians need in Congress.
#
Peter,
One of Chris Rabb’s biggest opponents in the heated primary race for Pennsylvania’s 3rd congressional district is absolutely floundering.
First, Dr. Ala Stanford denied any support from AIPAC. Dropsite News revealed it was a lie, and that **AIPAC donors are supporting Stanford’s campaign directly and through a shell PAC.**
Then, **Stanford awkwardly asked to pause an interview on live TV** because she didn’t know how to answer a question about who should enforce immigration laws if ICE is abolished.
Now, **she abruptly dropped out of today’s candidate debate** two hours before it was set to begin.
It’s beyond clear: _Stanford is not prepared to be the leader Philadelphians need in Congress._
Our candidate, State Rep. Chris Rabb, is.
He’s spent the last 8 years serving his majority-Black, mixed-income district and introducing bold legislation in the Pennsylvania House. He doesn’t take a cent from AIPAC or any other corporate PACs. And he wholeheartedly believes in a free Palestine, abolishing ICE, and passing progressive policies like Medicare for All.
Now that Stanford has made it clear she’s not a serious candidate in this race, **we need to give Chris as much grassroots support as possible to make sure he can defeat her and his other establishment opponent on May 19.**

| | | Dear Friend, The May 1st deadline is critical to ensuring we have the resources to communicate our message and reach voters before the election. If you’re able, please consider making a contribution today: [DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/IAuGCe8c4QN?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02) As a proud fourth-generation San Mateo County resident with over 20 years of public service, I’m running for Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder and Chief Elections Officer to modernize this office and restore confidence in how it serves our community. A prior review made it clear that stronger leadership, greater transparency, and improved trust are needed, and I’m ready to deliver. As a former Mayor and current member of the Board of Supervisors, I oversee a $5.5 billion organization with 5,800 employees and strong financial reserves. I understand that accountability, sound management, and collaboration are essential to delivering reliable public services. body: | | | | Oregon Republicans urge a NO vote on Measure 120 and returning ballots by May 19. --- --- Dear Patriot, Oregon Republicans are urging voters across the state to **vote NO on Measure 120** and return their Primary Election ballots by May 19. Measure 120 would impose a **massive $4.3 billion tax increase** —raising gas taxes, increasing vehicle registration and title fees, and doubling payroll taxes for public transit. If passed, Oregon’s gas tax would rise from 40 cents to 46 cents per gallon—among the highest in the nation. At a time when families are already feeling the pressure of rising costs, this measure would make life even more expensive for working Oregonians, commuters, seniors, and small businesses. --- **Key facts:** • $4.3 billion tax increase • Higher gas taxes and vehicle fees • Increased payroll taxes for transit • Ballots due May 19 --- We believe Oregonians deserve accountability, affordability, and responsible leadership—not another massive tax burden. 👉 Take action now: Vote NO on Measure 120.
