| | **Alaska** _**League of Women Voters of Alaska v. Dahlstrom**_**, No. 3-AN-26-____CI (Alaska Super. Ct.)** On April 22, advocacy groups [sued state election officials](https://us.list-manage.com/11bDEdEESKX?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), alleging that the state’s sharing of sensitive voter registration data with the Department of Justice violates constitutional privacy and due process protections.**Arizona** _**Public Interest Legal Foundation v. Fontes**_**, No. 2:25-cv-02772 (D. Ariz.)** On April 20, the Public Interest Legal Foundation [announced that it settled a federal lawsuit](https://us.list-manage.com/qO_f2c6jjmu?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) over access to voter roll maintenance records, with the state agreeing to produce data identifying voters mistakenly removed as deceased and to maintain those records for up to two years._**United States v. Fontes**_**, No. CV-26-00066 (D. Ariz.)** On April 28, a federal court [ruled](https://us.list-manage.com/9CHsEK4TsjX?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the DOJ cannot compel the state to turn over its full voter file._**Heap v. Galvin**_**, No. CV 2025-020621 (Ariz. Super. Ct., Maricopa Cnty.)** On April 17, a state court [ruled](https://us.list-manage.com/8mDUKWrl7Fa?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors unlawfully stripped authority over key election functions from the recorder’s office._**Strong Cmtys. Found. of Ariz., Inc. v. Yavapai Cnty.**_**, No. S1300CV202400175 (Ariz. Super. Ct., Yavapai Cnty.)** On April 23, the Arizona Court of Appeals [dismissed a lawsuit](https://us.list-manage.com/RR7PVhIIclV?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) challenging the state’s use of ballot drop boxes and certain signature verification procedures, holding the plaintiffs lacked standing to bring the claims.**Colorado** _**Colo. Republican Party v. Griswold**_**, No. 23-cv-01948-PAB (D. Colo.)** On April 20, the Colorado Republican Party [asked a federal court](https://us.list-manage.com/DJB4PYilZRx?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to block unaffiliated voters from participating in its 2026 primary, arguing that the state’s semi-open primary system violates the party’s associational rights. The court [denied the request](https://us.list-manage.com/Z7BTE8Hn6GE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on April 28.**District of Columbia** _**Common Cause v. United States**_**, No. 1:26-cv-01352 (D.D.C.)** On April 21, advocacy groups [sued in federal court](https://us.list-manage.com/xmHGEW64Lam?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to block the DOJ from obtaining and using state voter-registration data as part of its systemic list maintenance efforts.**Georgia** _**DeKalb Cnty. Bd. of Registrations and Elections v. State Election Bd.**_**, No. 24CV9085-10 (Ga. Super. Ct., Dekalb Cnty.)** On April 23, a state court invalidated two State Election Board rules governing daily vote reporting and poll watcher access as exceeding statutory authority, while dismissing challenges to a separate hand-counting rule as moot.**Hawaii** _**Public Interest Legal Found., Inc. v. Nago**_**, No. 1:23-cv-00389 (D. Haw.)** On April 28, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit [held](https://us.list-manage.com/15ItWfwmoaY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that Hawaii is not required under the National Voter Registration Act to disclose its statewide voter registration list to the Public Interest Legal Foundation (PILF), concluding that the statute’s public disclosure provision does not apply to voter rolls. The court did find that PILF had standing and that the case was ripe.**Indiana** _**Count Us In v. Morales**_**, No. 1:25-cv-00864 (S.D. Ind.)** On April 20, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit [stayed a district court injunction](https://us.list-manage.com/YPG1y3TE9eT?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) blocking the state ban on the use of student IDs for voting, allowing the law to take effect while early voting in the May 5 primary election continues.**Louisiana** _**Louisiana v. Callais,**_**No. 3:24-cv-00122 (W.D. La.)** On April 29, the [U.S. Supreme Court struck down](https://us.list-manage.com/UYi2SGvXG1F?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Louisiana’s congressional district map that would add a second majority-black district. The Court ruled that creating these districts [violates the Equal Protection Clause](https://us.list-manage.com/WmsIij4yLWs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of the 14th Amendment of the United States Constitution. **Massachusetts** _**California v. Trump**_**, No. 1:26-cv-11581 (D. clean_body: Arizona Experiments to Speed up Election Results - By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI - The 2020 president... | | | | | | | | | Arizona Experiments to Speed up Election Results By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI The 2020 presidential race . It took a week to determine which party controlled the House in . This phenomenon erodes voter confidence without any benefit that couldn’t be achieved by counting votes more quickly. Heavy vote-by-mail states may tend to report results more slowly, but the pace is largely the product of policy choices that some states make and others have not.The menu of reforms has been well understood and “pre-processing” ballots is perhaps the most cited. Pre-processing is a broad term encompassing the various steps election officials may take before Election Day to prepare mail ballots for final tabulation: removal of ballots from outer and inner envelopes, duplication of ballots that are not machine readable, ballot scanning, and identity verification. Although some experts suggest its impact may be overstated, it demonstrably speeds up getting totals, especially in the crucial window . Identity verification is a core component in the process. In-person voting confirms identity up front and most of those votes are recorded immediately. In contrast, mail ballots defer verification until after submission, through signature matching, review of ballot envelope affidavits, etc. Although aided by technology such as the Agilis machine in Clark County, Nevada, signature verification requires significant human judgment and takes time to do properly. Of course, this along with the rest of pre-processing must be complete before officials can tabulate and report results.Arizona verifies identity through signature matching. It’s also a laggard in reporting election results, which is problematic given the extremely tight 2020 presidential race there and subsequent close races in the national spotlight. Although Arizona pre-processes, its effectiveness is muted by an increasing trend of voters there returning ballots in-person near or on Election Day (so-called “late earlies”). Maricopa officials stated that of all votes cast there in the 2022 General Election were early ballots dropped off on Election Day. Officials then need to transport those ballots to a central location for processing (including signature verification), which results in Arizona processing fewer ballots before Election Day than in other states. A five-business-day ballot cure period for signature verification mismatches stretches the process further. In the upcoming election, Arizona will implement an innovative approach that may help. enacted in 2024 lets mail voters bypass signature matching by returning their ballot in person and presenting acceptable identification at a voting location. This could, in theory, speed up the process for counting Arizona’s mail ballots used by roughly 75% of the state’s voters. A recent article raises several caveats that may inhibit widespread adoption, including longer lines for voters who opt to show ID versus no lines for those who just drop them off. Nonetheless, this is an intriguing reform, and one adopted with broad bipartisan support, especially notable in a state beset by a rancorous partisan debate over elections policy. Although signature verification is better than no verification, it is not ideal. It simultaneously leads to the rejection of valid ballots and the acceptance of fraudulent ones. It also leads to more curing, which—again—further delays results and risks rejecting more ballots. Verifying mail voters’ identities through an objective identification standard is good for both access and integrity. If a voter goes to such trouble, why not just vote in-person? Most Arizonans are on a permanent absentee voting list and automatically receive a ballot, something unlikely to change anytime soon. The state is also known for lengthy ballots. Some voters may wish to complete their ballot at home at their own pace and then return it in person and avoid the risks of postal delivery delays and signature matching by using the ID verification option.Arizona is unlikely to be “Florida fast” in results reporting anytime soon but it’s at least proactively working on solutions. This is a good lesson in policymaking. Although implementing certain national best practices can produce quicker election results, solutions need to be tailored to each state’s idiosyncrasies and voting cultures. This legislation was. Maine Gov. Janet Mills ended her bid for the U.S. Senate on Thursday, abandoning a primary campaign that had collapsed under the weight of bad polling, a dry advertising pipeline and a restive Democratic base that never warmed to the candidate Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer personally recruited.
Mills waved the white flag in a X post Thursday morning.
[| | | | | Janet Mills
---
@JanetMillsforME
My statement suspending my candidacy for the U.S. Senate:
| 12:46 PM * Apr 30, 2026 * 90.6K Views89 Replies * 95 Reposts * 234 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/f91d0e17-16d5-4d85-9914-a800c44c9919?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Although Mills had won re-election to the Blaine House just four years ago, her popular support among Maine Democrats appeared to be a mirage, as she was never able to conjure a reliable base. Turnout at her public events resembled what you might expect for a local select-board candidate.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..kxktM0OVpj3dYvClsvKaJPJFw9ozagChN2GBv7GVG0Q?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=195994477)
Her exit, six weeks before the June 9 primary, effectively hands the Democratic nomination to Graham Platner, the disabled Marine Corps veteran with an oyster hobby whose insurgent campaign has dominated polling, fundraising and the airwaves since last summer. Platner will now face Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who is seeking a sixth term, in what is expected to be one of the most expensive and closely watched Senate races in the country.
Mills, 78, was the only Democrat to win a statewide race in Maine in the past two decades. She entered the contest in October with the full backing of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, a joint fundraising committee with national party leadership, and endorsements that read like a roster of the Democratic establishment.
None of it stuck. Or perhaps it even hurt.
Platner had been leading Mills in every public poll of the race, by margins that grew rather than narrowed after the governor's mid-March advertising blitz attacked his old Reddit posts and the Nazi tattoo that Platner has lied about multiple times.
By April, internal Democratic polling reviewed by national outlets put Platner ahead by as many as 38 points. Mills' campaign stopped booking television advertising after April 8, according to data from the ad-tracking firm AdImpact, and never resumed.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=195994477&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1OTk0NDc3LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc1NTQ5ODAsImV4cCI6MTc4MDE0Njk4MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.xEO_YF7J4HaEyCK2HrXrCAe1FVbx95dgiTOvpTN5F04)
For Schumer, the result is a public defeat in a primary he engineered. The Senate Democratic leader personally lobbied Mills to enter the race, and his campaign apparatus' close coordination with her bid prompted accusations of favoritism that Platner used to rally a small-dollar donor base and a volunteer operation his campaign says now numbers more than 15,000 active members.
The general election is now joined. Maine's June 9 primary remains on the ballot, with 2024 nominee David Costello and write-in candidate Andrea LaFlamme, a University of Maine adjunct professor, still in the field. Neither has registered measurable support in public polling.

_**Faith. Family. Freedom.**_

The Left is doing _everything_ they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored.

From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul.

**This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.**

Will you stand with me?

_The Cumberland County Superior Court has given the Secretary of State until May 26 to issue a new Determination of Validity. The Maine Girl Dads referendum -- and the November ballot question on whether boys belong in girls' sports and locker rooms -- now turns on what happens in Room 127 of the State House._
* * *
Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) signaled that she's once again maneuvering to undercut a popular ballot referendum, and, once again, organizers behind the ballot question committee may have given her an opening to do just that.
The Office of the Secretary of State announced Wednesday morning that it will hold an adjudicatory hearing on May 12 to take new evidence on the citizen-initiated petition to "Designate School Sports Participation and Facilities by Sex" -- the referendum better known to most Mainers as the Maine Girl Dads initiative.
The hearing is the direct consequence of an April 24 order from the Cumberland County Superior Court, which remanded _Gilbert v. Bellows_ back to the Secretary's office "for further proceedings consistent with this Order, which may include correcting the concessions identified [in the Court's decision and order], taking new evidence, and developing further findings of fact as necessary."
Translation: the court was not satisfied that Bellows got it right the first time, and it has handed her a tight calendar to fix it. The Secretary has been directed to issue a new Determination of Validity by May 26.

Although that might sound like a black eye for Bellows, it gives Maine's most nakedly partisan and self-serving election administrator another opportunity to winnow down the thin ~3,000 signature margin the Protect Girls Sports in Maine ballot question committee held once the Secretary of State certified their submission.
The group submitted [79,692 ](https://substack.com/redirect/21ca32ba-f0de-4ca8-bd8c-de60dc375256?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)petition signatures in February, but Bellows rejected 8,659 of those signatures for various reasons -- mostly to do with paid signature-gatherers not following proper procedures. Under Maine law, the requirement for signatures is based on the most recent gubernatorial election, which for 2026 would mean the committee needs 67,682 signatures -- a measure they exceeded by 3,351.
In claiming Bellows erred with her original certification, the court is effectively saying that an unknown number of those 3,351 signatures may also be suspect. If Bellows and the judicial branch conspire to bounce enough signatures from the re-certification, then the proposed protections for sex-based rights will not make the Nov. 2026 ballot.
The hearing will begin at 10:00 a.m. in Room 127 -- the Taxation Committee Room -- at the State House in Augusta. Chief Deputy Secretary of State Katherine McBrien will preside. Assistant Attorney General Jonathan Bolton, the same AAG whose Rule 80C brief is now being unwound on remand, will sit at the Chief Deputy's elbow as legal counsel. The proceeding will be live-streamed on the Department's YouTube page.
## What Happened
Cumberland County Superior Court Justice Deborah Cashman sent the case back to Secretary of State Shenna Bellows after three Mainers -- Jane Gilbert, Mark Sayre, and Kaitlin Webber -- filed a challenge on March 27.
Gilbert, Sayre, and Webber argued that Bellows had counted thousands of signatures that should have been thrown out. Their challenge was not based on a single defect but on a long list of alleged problems that, taken together, they said should disqualify the initiative from the ballot.
Their arguments included claims that petition organizations failed to register properly under Maine law, that out-of-state circulators failed to consent to Maine jurisdiction, that some circulators left petitions unattended and then falsely swore they had witnessed every signature, that some signatures were forged, that some notaries had conflicts of interest because they had also worked as circulators, and that many signatures had technical defects involving dates, addresses, or duplicate entries.
In layman's terms, the challenge threw everything at the wall to see what might stick. The petitioners' core legal theory was that Maine election statutes use mandatory language -- words like "shall" and "must" -- and that the Secretary cannot excuse defects by calling them minor or technical.
The case was filed under Rule 80C of the Maine Rules of Civil Procedure, which governs administrative appeals. The specific statutory authority is 21-A M.R.S. § 905, the section of Maine election law that allows voters to challenge the Secretary of State's determinations on initiative petitions.

This matters for understanding standing. Maine law gives any registered voter the right to challenge the Secretary's signature validation in Superior Court. The petitioners did not need to prove a personal injury beyond their status as Maine voters whose ballots would include -- or not include -- this initiative. The statute itself confers standing.
According to the Amended Notice of Hearing signed by McBrien on April 28, the parties may present evidence and argument on four buckets of issues, all of them lifted directly from the petitioners' challenges:
* **Challenge No. 2** -- whether circulators engaged in conduct contrary to their circulator's oath, and what the consequences should be for the signatures they collected;
* **Challenge Table 19a** -- whether 31 individual signatures flagged as "suspicious" by the petitioners should be invalidated;
* **Challenge No. 19** -- whether two specific circulators engaged in misconduct that taints the signatures they collected;
* **Challenges 3, 12, 14, 15, and 16** -- whether Bellows should walk back any of the concessions she made in her Rule 80C brief, including the live question of whether out-of-state circulators can be allowed to file _corrected_ personal-jurisdiction forms after the petition was already submitted to the state.

That last category is most significant for the Secretary's office. In Bolton's April 17 filing, the AG's office conceded that as many as 3,014 signatures Bellows' office had originally certified should have been invalidated. About half of those were collected by out-of-state circulators who failed to check the box on their affidavits consenting to Maine's personal jurisdiction. The rest were duplicates her office missed and signatures with date problems her office did not flag. The court's remand order tells her to revisit the question of whether she should be accepting after-the-fact "corrected" affidavits at all.
If you're doing the math at home, the clearance margin is now in the hundreds.
If the Secretary, on remand, sustains the concessions she has already made, the cushion shrinks significantly. If the hearing produces evidence that two specific circulators engaged in oath-breaking misconduct, or that a meaningful share of the 31 "suspicious" signatures were forged or witnessed in violation of the circulator's oath, the math tightens further.
One troubling sign for proponents of the referendum to protect sex-based rights in education is that paid signature collection is a notoriously sketchy business. The Protect Girls Sports in Maine committee is known to have used at least a few of the same contractors who derailed State Sen. Jim Libby (R-York)'s gubernatorial campaign by engaging in signature collection methods the Maine Ethics Commission described as fraudulent.
If those same contractors cut-corners, broke the rules, or outright forged signatures, Maine Girl Dad's will have to focus on gubernatorial and legislative elections, rather than a popular referendum, to keep gender dysphoric young men out of their daughters' locker rooms and athletic leagues.
## Witnesses, exhibits, and the May 1 cutoff
The hearing will be conducted under the Maine Administrative Procedure Act. Witnesses may appear in person or by video conference. Written affidavits will not be admitted unless the affiant is available for cross-examination -- a rule that has real bite given that much of Gilbert's case has, until now, been documented through affidavits, video, and photographs of unattended petition forms.
Witness lists and exhibit lists are due to the Secretary's office by Tuesday, May 5. The full Agency Record filed with the Superior Court on April 6 -- and supplemented by court order on April 24 -- will be admitted into the hearing record at the start of the proceeding. Closing arguments will be filed in writing.
Anyone seeking to intervene must file a written request with the Secretary, copying all parties, no later than 4:00 p.m. on Friday, May 1. (Tomorrow.)
Gilbert, Sayre, and Webber are represented by Christopher D. Dodge of the Elias Law Group out of Washington, D.C., and James Monteleone of Bernstein Shur in Portland. The Elias Law Group, for readers who haven't been keeping score, is the Marc Elias firm -- the same shop that has spent the better part of a decade helping the national Democratic Party litigate over election rules from coast to coast. It's also the same law firm Bellows has paid at least $12,000 via her gubernatorial campaign committee.
Protect Girls Sports (PGS) in Maine, the ballot question committee defending the petition, is represented by Timothy Woodcock of Katahdin Law in Bangor. PGS was permitted to intervene by the Superior Court in support of the petition's validity and will be a full party at the hearing.
The Secretary of State will be defended by AAG Bolton, who, in addition to advising the presiding officer, will be in the strange institutional posture of arguing for the validity of a determination his client has already partially conceded was wrong.
## What to watch on May 12
Three things are worth watching closely when the hearing convenes in Room 127.
First, the circulator-oath evidence. The petitioners have alleged that several circulators left petitions unattended -- meaning voters signed without the circulator present, in direct violation of the constitutional requirement that the circulator personally witness each signature. They have also alleged that two specific circulators may have outright forged signatures. Bolton has already conceded that those questions cannot be resolved on the paper record and require fact-finding. May 12 is the fact-finding.
Second, the "corrected forms" question. Whether the Secretary may allow out-of-state circulators to _retroactively_ check the box consenting to Maine personal jurisdiction -- a box they were required to check before submission -- goes to the integrity of the entire process. If the answer is yes, the rule effectively becomes meaningless. If the answer is no, somewhere on the order of 1,500 signatures collected by non-resident circulators come off the pile. That decision would also raise questions about the validity of signatures submitted for, well, basically everything that requires signatures. Again, the signature collection game is a dirty hustle. It almost always involves out-of-state hired guns loitering outside of grocery stores.
Third, the math. The petition crossed the threshold by 3,351 valid signatures. The Secretary has already conceded about 3,014. The hearing exists to resolve the rest -- the 31 "suspicious" signatures, the unattended-petition signatures, the alleged forgeries, and the contested categories in Challenges 12, 14, 15, and 16. There is no scenario in which May 12 does not directly determine whether Maine voters get to vote in November on whether boys belong in girls' sports.
The hearing will be livestreamed on the Department of the Secretary of State's YouTube page beginning at 10:00 a.m. on Tuesday, May 12. The Secretary's new Determination of Validity is due by May 26.
### The moral of the story: Don't hire scumbags and morons to do your signature collection.

Friend,
With just under three weeks until the primary, Team Wallace is building momentum on the campaign trail. Read on for campaign updates and how you can be part of the movement we're building together.
### **Three Ways To Get Involved This Week**
1. **Make your plan to vote on or before May 19.** Check out [this resource](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/dc12f55f-4abc-4785-b17e-4b6f06687266?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) if you're planning to vote by mail.
2. **Reach out to three people about voting.** Talk to people in your life about the primary - make sure they request a ballot by May 12 if they are not planning to vote in person on May 19. And tell them about Rachel and her campaign!
3. **Sign up for a canvassing shift.** Talking directly to voters is a great way to get people out to vote for the primary. Bring a friend, enjoy getting some steps in, and tell people why you're voting for Rachel. Check out the volunteer opportunities section below for a list of canvass options this weekend!

### **What We 've Been Up To**
We've been busy this past week! Here's a recap of the events Rachel and Team Wallace attended this week.
**[Susquehanna Meet and Greet](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ae716a94-97d8-4886-beb3-d52d1b79e40c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Rachel joined the folks of Great Bend at the VFW on Friday evening for a conversation about why she's in the race, the stakes for the district, and how [Dan Meuser profited off taxpayer-funded Medicare dollars, then voted to rip our health care away.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7e2bc1a7-430a-4366-87d4-3733c35783f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**[Bradford County Conversation](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/578fd3eb-1c09-4a36-97d3-33a304e1db66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Voters joined Rachel in Athens on Saturday to talk about housing, health care, and how to fix our broken politics. Thanks to everyone who came out in the rain!
**[Endless Mountains Maple Festival](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cd2b9960-f472-416c-afdf-b1037ca7462b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The rain didn't stop us from hanging out at Endless Mountains Maple Festival in Troy on Saturday! We loved the maple lemonade from Jelliff's - make it at home by combining a cup of maple syrup, a cup of real lemon juice concentrate, and 6 cups of water.
**[Susquehanna County Farm Bureau Conversation](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f64e20d6-b4d8-4044-9888-aae15c42c887?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Rachel joined the Susquehanna County Farm Bureau on Friday to talk about prioritizing health care access for our rural communities.
[](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a53827b5-3ef2-4ccf-af91-b01f85f842e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**If you have events in your area you 'd like to invite Rachel to, please get in touch with us at [info@wallaceforcongress.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d5976541-fae7-4f41-af17-4487756da3c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
### **[📢 Get Involved:](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fb6f67ab-709a-42ce-af35-8312a4b2e0fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Upcoming Events with Rachel**
* **Sat., May 2:**
* **Danville Spring Fling:** Join Rachel at the Danville Spring Fling around lunchtime! The Spring Fling is an all-ages outdoor event featuring downtown and area businesses, plus more than 200 vendors including food trucks, craft vendors selling their handmade wares, activities for the kids, and bands rocking the Canal Park stage. **[More information here.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/834fb025-080b-4e8e-9a52-60d6c8327071?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Wyoming Lackawanna County Farm Bureau Dinner:** Join Rachel at 6 PM at the Nicholson Methodist Church (64 State St, Nicholson PA 18446.)
* **Sun., May 3:**
* **Columbia County Democrats Spring Brunch:** Join Rachel and the Columbia County Democrats for breakfast -- great candidates and good food included! [RSVP here.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/aaa62d13-da89-4f12-890c-d5db727ee077?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Join Steve as he interviews John Strand who Amid COVID lockdowns and BLM violence, organized and led a freedom rally, which President Trump tweeted to support, and then became the Creative Director and national spokesperson for America's Frontline Doctors during one of the most polarized periods in modern American history. That courage came at a steep personal cost.
During a hostile administration, John Strand experienced firsthand what happens when government power goes unrestrained. He was assaulted by an FBI SWAT team, held in jail for four days without a phone call, and charged with a 20-year felony -- without any actual evidence of wrongdoing. Prosecutors offered him an easy exit: plead guilty to a single misdemeanor, sign a false confession, and go home. He refused. Rather than bear false witness and betray his fellow Americans, he chose to face the full weight of a weaponized government. John was sentenced to nearly three years and spent 366 days in a higher-security federal prison.
But the story did not end there. John was vindicated by the Supreme Court and released. John continued his appeal and ultimately achieved total exoneration of all charges. Rather than breaking him, the experience strengthened his resolve. That is why John Strand is running for Congress. For more about John visit [www.johnstrand.com](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f373c2-35a0-46b2-ba92-2af171368357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Friend — A couple months ago, a very unwell man tried to attack Ilhan at a town hall meeting in Minneapolis. He rushed Ilhan’s podium while spraying her with liquid from a syringe.
Thankfully, Ilhan’s security apprehended the man almost immediately. He was charged at the federal level with assaulting and interfering with a U.S. officer, and at the local level with felony terroristic threats and fifth-degree assault. He is set to plead guilty.
This attack came as no surprise to those of us who have seen what Trump has said about Ilhan, and how the entire GOP has put a target on Ilhan’s back.
Trump has called Ilhan “garbage,” mocked her hijab, said she should “get the hell out” and “go back” to Somalia, and even joked about working with Somali officials to deport her. JD Vance has accused Ilhan of fraud and illegal acts without a shred of evidence. Republicans in Congress have circulated petitions calling for her to be denaturalized and removed from the country. They’ve opened sham investigations to try to intimidate her.
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-apr26.yEIO3a&refcode=em260430-1-180&t=3&akid=2196%2E791427%2EFv_Ss6)
And here’s the thing: **Congress does not provide Ilhan with a security team.** That’s something our campaign has to pay for, and we are extremely thankful that our security team was there that day to protect her.
But this attack hasn’t deterred Trump's dangerous rhetoric even a bit. The targeting has continued, and Trump has even claimed that the attack was a setup by Ilhan herself.
That’s why we’re reaching out to you. Tonight is our April fundraising deadline. What we raise today will decide our budget going forward, and that budget includes our security team. We’re asking for your help to keep Ilhan on the campaign trail and in the fight against MAGA.

I wish I had better news, but I wanted you to hear this directly from me: We’re behind.
#

Friend:
My team and I have written to you about our goal for this month a few times, and with our deadline tonight, I thought I should update you on our progress.
I wish I had better news, but I wanted you to hear this directly from me: We’re behind. Not so far behind that we have no chance at catching up, but behind nonetheless.
So, we have two options ahead of us. Either we come together over the next several hours and make some real progress toward these goals, or we don’t.
To be clear: The sky is not going to fall if we miss these goals. I’m not going to blow this out of proportion and try to scare you into donating. That’s not what this is about, because that’s not the kind of team we’ve built.
What missing these goals means is rolling back some of the plans we’ve made this year. With elections in November and a potential Senate majority at stake, there could be real consequences to that.
Friend, you know me. I have never been one to sit on the sidelines, and this is no different. After the polls close, I don’t want to look back and wonder what more I could’ve done.
I’ll take this work on myself if I have to, but I know we’ll accomplish a lot more if we do it together. So, please:

Since I launched my campaign for Missouri’s 1st Congressional District last year, people have asked:
“Cori, why would you even want to go back to that chaos?”
And my answer is simple. Because I’m going to finish what I started.
I didn’t come this far just to leave the work undone. The work our movement fought for. The work our communities deserve.
I co-founded and co-chaired the first Equal Rights Amendment Caucus in Congress. And I’m not done.
Peter, the political moment we’re in right now doesn’t call for caution; it calls for bold, unapologetic leadership.
I’m going back to Congress to finish what I started: To enshrine the right to abortion in the Constitution, deliver reparations for the descendants of enslaved Africans, pass Medicare for All, abolish ICE, achieve real accountability in policing, stand up for the people of Gaza, and so much more.
This isn’t about going back. It’s about going forward with the same urgency, the same courage, and the same communities that got us here in the first place.

| Peter,

I'm writing my Constitutional Law final exam, and I figured I'd send you an update while I take a short break.

Our Constitution is pretty clear on what the House is supposed to do. In Article I, our founders outlined a chamber of Congress with the power to check both the executive branch and the Senate through the "power of the purse," oversight hearings, veto overrides, and more.

But unfortunately, the leadership in today's House of Representatives, including Mariannette Miller-Meeks, is refusing to use those powers to safeguard our democracy. They're more concerned with representing special interests and party agendas than the very people who sent them to Washington. As I travel the district, it is clear that people are getting tired of having no _real_ representation in Congress.

Iowans know Mariannette Miller-Meeks is their “representative,” but more and more, they're asking whether that representation is actually showing up for them in a meaningful way. **At the end of the day, actions speak louder than titles, and Miller-Meeks' actions aren't delivering for the people of IA-01.**

That's why we're trying to show voters something different.

Rain or shine — and if you've seen Iowa's weather lately, you know it's been a whole lot of rain — I have been out meeting people where they are and having honest conversations about their concerns, their hopes, and what they want to see from their leaders. Those conversations mean everything to me. And we're not slowing down anytime soon.

November might feel far away, but we're already deep in the second quarter of the year. Right now, we have our first big opportunity of the quarter to make an impact and set the tone for what's ahead.Reaching our monthly fundraising goal will help us expand our outreach and continue these conversations across the district. Team: The Supreme Court’s six-to-three conservative majority issued a staggering ruling yesterday that essentially kills the remaining protections of the Voting Rights Act , dealing a death blow to the country’s most important civil rights law.
The majority opinion by Justice Samuel Alito in Louisiana v. Callais strikes down the congressional map in Louisiana and in doing so " narrows Section 2 of the VRA to the point of irrelevance, making it nearly impossible to prove that a gerrymandered map violates the right of voters of color ."
The impact shows how partisan this all is. This decision harms only one political party to the direct benefit of the other and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we thought we left behind sixty years ago.
What can we do to respond? It sounds simple, but just get back to work informing voters, reengaging lapsed voters, registering new ones, and turning out everyone we can for the midterms and beyond.

Justice Elena Kagan put it simply and correctly. What remains is a “dead letter.”** That means the protections that stopped discriminatory maps and voter suppression are now hanging by a thread. And you can expect what comes next. More extreme and aggressive redistricting here in Texas and across the South. **The damage from MAGA extremism is real.** But I am not going to sit here and tell you there is nothing we can do. Because that’s not true. **We can register every high school senior in Texas under existing law.** That’s roughly 500,000 new voters every year. Over one term, that’s 2 million new voices. **We can register Texans when they interact with state services** , including Child Support Division offices. That’s another million people brought into the process. And every single day, **we can use the power of this office to encourage participation instead of suppressing it.** To make voting easier instead of harder. # **Former Minnesota police officer reveals fraud allegation coverup, Tim Walz shut down his department**
Former Minnesota DHS criminal investigator Jay Swanson testified Tuesday that **[his bosses ordered him to delete fraud findings](https://substack.com/redirect/b484a122-0eeb-4276-ab2e-855a09c13cc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in response to a legislative inquiry and that it was "common knowledge among Somali refugees in camps in Kenya that Minnesota was the best place to operate a scam." A DHS official barged into his office "angry, red-faced, and almost yelling" telling him to retract fraud allegations, with Swanson saying the request was "illegal." DHS later paid $90,000 to a consulting firm with "no experience" in fraud investigations to discredit his findings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b484a122-0eeb-4276-ab2e-855a09c13cc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Walz administration allegedly shut down investigations** : Republican lawmakers say when Gov. Tim Walz took office in 2019, his administration shut down the DHS Office of Inspector General, telling investigators "they could no longer do criminal investigations" without supervisors' approval. The Trump administration estimates the fraud could total $9-19 billion, with 98 people charged since 2022, 85 of Somali descent.
* **Walz claims credit after FBI raids** : After FBI raided nearly two-dozen daycares, Walz--who dismissed allegations as "white supremacy"--wrote "If you commit fraud in Minnesota you're going to get caught." FBI Director Kash Patel fired back: "go ahead and take credit for our work while we smoke out the fraud plaguing Minnesota under your governorship."

* * *
# **Michigan city removes 600+ neighborhood watch signs to be more "inclusive," draws widespread mockery**
Democrat-dominated Ann Arbor, Michigan **[completed citywide removal of over 600 neighborhood watch signs](https://substack.com/redirect/100da731-b87d-4077-8f01-a80a9a8187db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** this week after a unanimous 10-0 City Council vote in December, with the city saying "removing the signs aligns the city's environment with its commitment to inclusive, evidence-based public safety."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/100da731-b87d-4077-8f01-a80a9a8187db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Democratic Mayor Christopher Taylor said** in an official video that "neighborhood watch signs are expressions of exclusion," while the resolution claimed the programs "were often rooted in assumptions about who did and did not 'belong' in a neighborhood, reinforcing race-based hyper-vigilance and suspicion particularly toward Black, Brown, and other marginalized residents."
* **City spent $18,000 from cash reserves** : The City Council allocated $18,000 for sign removal, with officials revealing that removing non-traffic-related signs didn't qualify for street funding, and because no funds were available in the police budget, the city drew from cash reserves.
* **Conservatives slam move** : Former Michigan GOP gubernatorial candidate Tudor Dixon said "for years the Democrats have demanded community policing over police funding, but today they have hit a new level of protecting the criminal over the community," adding "There was a time Democrats believed it took a village to raise a child, and now they believe that village is racist."

# If you live in Nampa's District 13
### ... or know someone who does, read this.
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Apr 30
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
Check this out...
May 19th there's a Republican primary. Both candidates are Republican, which means whoever wins this race will 100% win the general election against the woke Democrat in November. Because this is a safe Republican district. So this primary is actually the election (the one that matters).
So whoever comes out of May 19th a winner will represent you at the statehouse.
For the first time ever, I don't have a Republican challenger. Because the governor and his minions got curb-stomped every time they ran against me and learned their lesson. But my friend Steve Tanner (rep District 13)?
He has a Republican challenger.
And you've probably already seen the other guy's ads. They're everywhere online. AI-generated, kinda generic. The weird part? He's running on stuff my friend Steve Tanner already believes and is already doing.
Which raises the question... _why is he running?_
Brad Little's endorsement answers that pretty cleanly.
Governors don't back candidates who are going to give them headaches. They back whoever they can count on to play ball when it matters. That's the whole calculation and the endorsement tells you everything about what this guy is expected to do once he gets there.
_**My friend Steve doesn 't have the Governor's blessing and that's kind of the point. **_
We've fought together on illegal immigration and he already knows where he stands before anyone gets a chance to lobby him. He answers to the people in District 13, full stop.
The other guy got Brad Little's endorsement and can't be bothered to read the state GOP platform, let alone sign it. He said that last night at a candidate forum! That combination should tell you something about who he's actually planning to answer to once he's in the legislature.
Bottom line: vote for my good friend Steve Tanner on **May 19th**.
Cheers,
Brian
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6f3b0f7c-805a-417f-a7a2-eca643bbf1e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**P.S.** Make sure you're registered to vote. You can [check your status here](https://substack.com/redirect/1a420f3c-e8c7-4d08-9405-55e3db330c31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**P.P.S.** Steve was the only Idaho representative who showed up at the border with me last week. While his challenger's got a slick AI ad talking tough about it, Steve was actually there. He won't bow to the illegal labor lobby and they know it. Maybe that's exactly why they're spending all this money trying to replace him?
(C) 2026 Brian Lenney

subject: Have You Voted for Me?
body:
This is the final days, next week is election day and we need your vote!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/fb7dba938c92/we-need-your-help-18006687?e=72dace1453)

|

|

| | | | |
---
| |
# The Final 5 Days!
---
| | Hello everyone, I am sure you are tired of the ads, the campaigning, the calls for action, and everything else but we need your help these last 5 days! Please, please, please go out and vote, get your neighbor to vote, tell your family to vote, and tell people about our campaign and our efforts to win this seat. I have been working hard 6 days a week the last 2 years to provide accountability, meet with voters, and ensure i can be the best representative of this district. I humbly ask for your vote next week and please reach out if there’s anything else you want to do to help!
---
|
---
| |
# I Need your Help at the Polls!
---
| | We now have 5 days left until election day! Now I am going to ask for your help to get our message out there! We are looking anyone available who can stand outside a polling station in one of our shirts and encourage people to vote for the Haggard for Congress Campaign! If you are interested, please contact me here, on Facebook or if you have my number, give me a text! The momentum is swinging towards us every day!
---
|
---
|
---
| | I will continue highlighting the endorsements I continue to receive throughout the district from local leaders and groups that put their faith in me to represent them in Congress. Our momentum is just getting started and I can’t wait to continue to share with you who is already on board. If you ever want to get involved or endorse, please reach out!
---

Did you know? + Campaign Fundraising Update | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/lwfaa/icymi-kelvin-king-for-ga-sec-of-state-14199475?e=cb396c52a2)

| |
---
| |
# Did you know?

During early voting, **Ballot on Demand** ensures you’ll never face a ballot shortage or receive the wrong precinct's paperwork. When you check in, a high-security printer generates a blank, official ballot tailored specifically to your residence. You then mark your choices by hand, maintaining the gold standard of election integrity with a physical paper trail. It’s a secure, efficient way to guarantee every voter’s voice is accurately captured and counted.
---
| |
# **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
## **Leading in Fundraising, Volunteers, and Momentum! **
We've heard that momentum is a force multiplier. Right now, our "flight path" is clear: **We are winning.** The polls show it, and the airwaves prove it. If you turn on your TV or fire up a streaming app, mine is the only SOS campaign you see. In a down-ballot race crowded with candidates, visibility is the entire game, so we are covering all sides. I have "skin in the game, too." I’ve invested a significant amount of my own money into my race and can make you a direct promise: **Every dollar you give now goes directly to voter contact.** As we speak, we are hitting **one million voters** to ensure they know exactly who to vote for. But I’m not content with texting them once. I would like to launch a final mass text-message blitz to ensure our message is the last thing they see before they head to the polls. **It will cost exactly $15,000 to execute this final strike. Will you help me fuel it?** Whether it’s $5, $50, or $500, your support at the end of this quarter sends a clear message to the media and our opponents: this movement cannot be stopped. We have the lead. Now we need the fuel to finish the mission. **Aim High,**

Friend —

I want to tell you something honest about why I’m running for Lieutenant Governor.

It’s not because I’m done with my work on the Providence City Council. I’m not. I love that work. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together in Ward 3 — and the whole City. But here’s what I’ve learned from doing it: the more you get done, _the more clearly you can see how much more there is to do and where it needs to happen._

From my seat on the City Council, I wrote and then passed an ordinance requiring all municipal buildings to be carbon neutral by 2040. I wrote and passed the resolution to ensure that Providence became the first Climate Jobs City in the country. We paired that commitment to clean energy with real union labor standards — because how you do the work matters as much as getting it done.

We fought for upgrades to infrastructure, traffic safety, and housing stability.

And every single time we won something, I thought: _this works. But it’s not enough. What am I going to do about it?_

The Lieutenant Governor’s office should be more than a backup plan for Gov. and someone to attend ribbon cuttings. It should be a force for _progress_. A place where Rhode Islanders can show up and have real input and impact on the important issues facing our state — and where we make real change happen.

That’s what I want to build.

clean_body: For this entire state | | | | Midnight Deadline: Tonight Goal: 57 Donors Short Team: ** | | Friend — I want to tell you something honest about why I’m running for Lieutenant Governor. It’s not because I’m done with my work on the Providence City Council. I’m not. I love that work. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together in Ward 3 — and the whole City. But here’s what I’ve learned from doing it: the more you get done, the more clearly you can see how much more there is to do and where it needs to happen. From my seat on the City Council, I wrote and then passed an ordinance requiring all municipal buildings to be carbon neutral by 2040. I wrote and passed the resolution to ensure that Providence became the first Climate Jobs City in the country. We paired that commitment to clean energy with real union labor standards — because how you do the work matters as much as getting it done. We fought for upgrades to infrastructure, traffic safety, and housing stability. And every single time we won something, I thought: this works. But it’s not enough. What am I going to do about it? The Lieutenant Governor’s office should be more than a backup plan for Gov. and someone to attend ribbon cuttings. It should be a force for progress. A place where Rhode Islanders can show up and have real input and impact on the important issues facing our state — and where we make real change happen. That’s what I want to build. One month ago, this election turned on its head

Derek, I owe you an explanation. Over the last few days, you’ve probably heard my team and I stress the importance of reaching our April fundraising goal — well, more than a few times. So I wanted to use this opportunity to show you exactly why this deadline matters. **As of 4 minutes ago, we still need more than 475 individual donations before midnight to hit our goal — and whether or not we reach that number will have a direct impact on our campaign operations from now until Election Day.** One month ago, this election turned on its head, Derek. Donald Trump — who’s already officially endorsed my opponent — took it to the next level. He personally appeared at a Mar-a-Lago fundraiser for my opponent, wining and dining with some of the most extreme, far-right donors in the entire country. _And it worked._ That fundraiser was confirmation: **Pennsylvania is at the very top of the far-right’s wish list — and they’re willing to spend millions to try and take it for themselves.** Here’s where our fundraising goals come in. You won’t see me traveling to Mar-a-Lago any time soon, schmoozing with Donald Trump. But elections take resources, Derek. And since those resources _definitely_ aren’t coming from Mar-a-Lago... name: Jason Crow
subject: This is our moment
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jason Crow for Congress
body:
We’re in a fight to save our democracy and everything is riding on what we do next. Will you join me in this fight? |
#

name: Wes Moore
subject: The grifting must stop.
body:
The citizens of Maryland deserve a truthful and honest government
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1344%2E1086043%2Ed4xBpp)
I have some news about how we’re fighting corruption in Maryland -- **[but our end-of-month deadline is at midnight tonight, so if you’re already on board with our work, please chip in right away.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260430-1.hyq_Fn&refcode=em-20260430-1&t=2&akid=1344%2E1086043%2Ed4xBpp)**
Every phase of my life has been guided by the principle of service to others, and if there’s one thing I know to be true, Peter, it’s this:
**When you step into a position of public trust, you leave your personal interests at the door.**
Unfortunately, right now, _some_ public officials are using their insider knowledge -- about legislation, national security, government policy -- to place bets on prediction markets. To profit from the very decisions they’re making on _your behalf._
_That’s just wrong._
You deserve a government where state business is conducted truthfully and honestly -- free from corruption or misconduct. **So that’s why I signed an executive order banning anyone in Maryland state government from using insider knowledge to place bets on prediction markets.**
This is just one order, but it’s part of how we’re leading with our values. The only way we continue that work -- and doing it at the scale this moment demands -- is with a strong grassroots team behind us.
**[I have my very first end-of-month fundraising deadline of 2026 tonight at midnight. If you can, will you chip in $5 or more to help us reach our $10,000 goal before time runs out?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260430-1.hyq_Fn&refcode=em-20260430-1&t=3&akid=1344%2E1086043%2Ed4xBpp)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260430-1.hyq_Fn&amount=5&refcode=em-20260430-1&t=22&akid=1344%2E1086043%2Ed4xBpp)**
Thank you, Peter. I’m grateful for this team.
-- Wes

**[Volunteer »](https://support.wesmoore.com/a/volunteer?source=em-20260430-1)**

clean_body: Are you on board? | = Friend, my 88 years have shown me it takes people power to win anything worthwhile. Every victory we’ve had since I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC — from electing 240 climate leaders nationwide to flipping over 60 seats last year — has come from our collective power. And that power is possible because people like you understand the stakes, get organized, and choose to back real leaders who will fight for the kind of future we urgently need. That future, a better future with better leaders, is on the line. You see, our opponents see the strength of this grassroots team, so they’re rewriting the rules and spending whatever is necessary to buy power. I refuse to let them get away with this, which is why I’m turning to you for help one more time before tonight’s deadline. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = I’ll be honest with you: I’ve heard “no” a lot over my decades of activism. “No, the women’s liberation movement will never accomplish anything.” “No, the anti-war movement will never actually stand up to the war machine.” “No, a grassroots movement can never beat Big Oil’s money and influence or beat back authoritarianism.” To every “no”, I say:Tell us we can’t do something, and we’ll work together to prove otherwise. Because the truth is, we’re already doing it: Earlier this month, our Clean Energy Slate flipped Arizona’s Salt River Project Board — one of the largest public utilities in the country. They beat one of the most well-funded, well-organized far-right groups in the country — Turning Point — with a record number of votes. That’s what grassroots power looks like. So when I tell you that we’re creating better, one person, one action, one voter at a time, believe me. You are powering this change. But change doesn’t just happen overnight. It takes each and every one of us investing in these candidates as early as we can to give them the strategic advantage they need over their corporate-backed opponents. = Thank you for everything you do. In solidarity, Jane xx | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. body:
cadem.org [cadem.org]
California Democrats,
With ballots dropping next week for the Primary Election, every day is Election Day through June 2. The California Democratic Party has a winning strategy to flip seats and take back the House, and it includes YOU.
From fighting for a more affordable future to protecting immigrant communities and defending our democracy, we're leading the fight to move our nation forward. The future we believe in is worth fighting for— will you join us to get out the vote?
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/412F544A32524E6948494C797470636E70587776545562436A58554E6C686E6A2F4D324F54507364445848352F774C43764C4E36447A486C6651583664617A2F/editor_images/OIA%20ICYMI%20Banner.png]
cadem.org/may16 [cadem.org/may16]
Last week, we launched our California Fights Forward: Statewide Day of Action [http://cadem.org/May16] —a day for all of us across the state to come together and do our part to get out the vote for the June 2 election. We're thrilled to invite you to partner with us on May 16th!
There are several ways you can participate in the Statewide Day of Action:
* Add your local phone bank or canvass to the "California Fights Forward: Statewide Day of Action" Mobilize campaign. [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/c/sample/event/create/] This will ensure your event, including local priority races, appears in our event directory.
* Volunteer at a CADEM canvass [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=30964&zoom=5]
* Volunteer at a CADEM virtual phone bank [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/?from_map=true&lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=30964&zoom=5]
Last Tuesday's Digital Organizing Training included a panel discussion moderated by CADEM Digital Director, Andrea Guzman, and content creators Timisola Ogunleye and Jessica Craven. We had a dynamic conversation about the importance of digital organizing, and how utilizing social media to organize is critical in today's political world.
cadem.org/train2026 [cadem.org/train2026]
Last week's California Latino Coalition meeting included a round-table discussion with the CADEM Latino Caucus and civic organizations. In partnership with these activists and organizations, we're mobilizing volunteers for our Spanish language phone banks that will launch in May. Together is how we'll win!
https://cadem.org/vote/ [https://cadem.org/vote/]
With the June 2 Primary Election right around the corner, we want to equip you with the tools you need to make a voting plan and ensure those around you are registered and ready for Election Day! Check out CADEM's online endorsement tool [https://cadem.org/our-endorsements/] to find endorsed Democrats where you live, and visit our Voter Information page [https://cadem.org/vote/] to find all the resources you need to vote.
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/412F544A32524E6948494C797470636E70587776545562436A58554E6C686E6A2F4D324F54507364445848352F774C43764C4E36447A486C6651583664617A2F/editor_images/OIA%20Upcoming%20Trainings%20Banner.png]
cadem.org/train2026 [cadem.org/train2026]
Join our free, online monthly organizing training series to learn the latest tools and strategies needed to flip seats and take back the House.
Register for our Monthly Training Series! [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/875048/]
https://politicaldata.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_nJrERPY5RbyFOntBphQr5w#/registration [https://politicaldata.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_nJrERPY5RbyFOntBphQr5w#/registration]
Join us for a special PDI Training: Texting and Campaign to Your Friends on April 30th at 3PM. This session will include special training on PDI's texting tools—both the peer-to-peer system and broadcast sending.
Register for PDI Training [https://politicaldata.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_nJrERPY5RbyFOntBphQr5w#/registration]
https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/917181/ [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/917181/]
Looking for a way to get involved in defending our democracy and cutting Donald Trump's term in half? Join our volunteer intro call to find out how you can get involved!
Join our next California Fights Forward: 2026 Team Briefing [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/917181/]
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/412F544A32524E6948494C797470636E70587776545562436A58554E6C686E6A2F4D324F54507364445848352F774C43764C4E36447A486C6651583664617A2F/editor_images/OIA%20Take%20Action%20Banner.png]
https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=30964&zoom=5 [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=30964&zoom=5]
Whether it’s calling voters or knocking on doors, we need you with us in the last two weeks before the June 2 Primary Election to make sure every vote counts! Fight Forward with us on our May 16 Statewide Day of Action to help get out the vote across California.
Join the Statewide Day of Action [cadem.org/may16]
https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/947093/ [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/947093/]
Join us every Wednesday from 5:30-7:30 PM as we call Spanish-speaking voters in our targeted Congressional districts to talk about the issues that matter most to them!
Call Spanish-speaking voters! [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/947093/]
https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/ [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/]
Join us every Tuesday and Thursday evening at 5:30pm from the comfort of your couch to make calls to voters in opportunity congressional districts.
Call voters! [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/]
https://www.mobilize.us/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=29029&zoom=5&nvep=&hmac=&emci=5c012296-53eb-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid= [https://www.mobilize.us/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=29029&zoom=5&nvep=&hmac=&emci=5c012296-53eb-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid=]
Join us this weekend to knock on doors and talk to voters in critical congressional districts across the state.
Knock on doors! [https://www.mobilize.us/map/?lat=36.7378&lon=-119.7871&tag_ids=29029&zoom=5&nvep=&hmac=&emci=5c012296-53eb-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid=]
https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/ [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/]
Every Monday, we call voters to help build up our volunteer base needed to take back the House! Every volunteer we recruit and every conversation we have with voters between now and Election Day matters—join us!
Recruit volunteers! [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/]
Every conversation between now and Election Day matters. Let's make the next 33 days count. I'll see you in the field!
- Helen Amelga
CADEM Organizing & Training Director

_**The bad news:**_ Trump cut $1.1 billion for public media outlets that he and Congress had earlier agreed to, **and this ruling doesn’t automatically guarantee that broadcasters will receive the funding they need to function.**

Their plan is to gerrymander this state back to the Reign of Terror.
Today, I woke up feeling like we are fighting the same fight my parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents fought, and it is this fight that makes America great. America was made great by the people who resisted, persisted, and fought for their freedom and right to a life of dignity.
We are going to fight like hell to make sure that these people who want to rig elections, gerrymander maps, take away elected black men's seats, and dilute black votes know that their time is up, and we are not going back.
I'm Jamie Davis, and I'm the Louisiana farmer and Democrat running to unseat MAGA Senator Bill Cassidy.

clean_body: When they can't win, they bend and break the rules. | | | | | == Peter, The MAGA Extremist Governor of Louisiana must think he is some kind of king or emperor, because he just called in a meeting with Republicans to postpone our upcoming election so he can have his cronies at the state capitol redraw maps. This is the Republican playbook: when they know they can't win, they bend, and then break, the rules. Word on the street in New Orleans is that Gov. Jeff Landry is going to completely eliminate one or even both districts represented by Troy Carter or Cleo Fields, both Black U.S. Representatives from Louisiana. | == With the Voting Rights Act gutted by the recent Supreme Court decision, Republican-run states are rushing to redraw maps to eliminate Black representatives. And unfortunately, Louisiana is no stranger to racist voter suppression, so I am sad to say that the news I share today comes as no surprise. First, they came for Calvin Duncan and moved to eliminate his clerk of court seat; and now they are coming for the state's only two majority-minority districts represented by two Black men in Congress. And who are they coming for next? Black voters. Their plan is to gerrymander this state back to the Reign of Terror. Today, I woke up feeling like we are fighting the same fight my parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents fought, and it is this fight that makes America great. America was made great by the people who resisted, persisted, and fought for their freedom and right to a life of dignity. We are going to fight like hell to make sure that these people who want to rig elections, gerrymander maps, take away elected black men's seats, and dilute black votes know that their time is up, and we are not going back. The year 2025 will be remembered as a watershed moment in government contracting, largely thanks to the Department of Government Efficiency's revolutionary approach to federal acquisition. What began as a controversial presidential initiative evolved into a powerful force for fiscal responsibility, saving taxpayers nearly $1 billion while delivering lessons in procurement innovation that will shape government operations for decades to come.

The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), established early in 2025, was tasked with an ambitious mandate: identify and eliminate wasteful spending throughout the federal procurement system. Led by former business leaders and efficiency experts, DOGE approached its mission not with random cost-cutting, but with systematic analysis of government contracts across all departments.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=195792061&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1NzkyMDYxLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc1Njg1NzcsImV4cCI6MTc4MDE2MDU3NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.jYAin4yOSX-8e498smM65gwTP_hs49pg4iffiss95-Q)
According to Washington Technology's analysis of DOGE's impact, the initiative "was government contracting's biggest story in 2025, and it's not close." This assessment reflects how comprehensively DOGE changed the conversation around federal spending.

The first major breakthrough came in early 2025 when federal agencies implemented DOGE's recommendations to cut 103 contracts, resulting in immediate savings of $103 million, as reported by Executive Gov. These weren't reckless cuts but strategic terminations of poorly performing, redundant, or overpriced agreements that had escaped scrutiny for years.

Perhaps more impressive was DOGE's success in identifying and eliminating 55 contracts with a combined ceiling value of $863 million. As GovCon Wire detailed, these cancellations represented the most significant consolidation of federal procurement activity in recent history. What made these cuts particularly noteworthy was their precision--targeting long-standing inefficient contracts without affecting necessary services

Beyond simple contract cancellations, DOGE introduced game-changing procurement methodologies that prioritized value over tradition. The initiative championed:

** **Data-driven decision making** **: Implementing advanced analytics to identify poorly performing contracts and cost overruns before they became problematic.
** **Performance-based contracting** **: Shifting focus from process compliance to actual results, with clearer metrics and accountability mechanisms.
** **Strategic sourcing** **: Encouraging interagency collaboration to leverage purchasing power across the government ecosystem.
** **Streamlined acquisition processes** **: Reducing administrative burdens that had historically inflated contract costs by up to 15%-20%.
Critics initially warned that DOGE's aggressive efficiency targets would harm government services and disrupt important programs. However, the evidence from 2025 tells a different story. By carefully analyzing contract performance data and focusing on eliminating redundancy rather than reducing essential services, DOGE managed to cut costs while maintaining-- and in some cases improving--service delivery.

A particularly compelling example comes from the Department of Health and Human Services, where DOGE helped consolidate 12 separate IT maintenance contracts into three more efficient agreements. This consolidation saved approximately $21 million annually while actually improving system uptime and user satisfaction scores.

The financial savings delivered by DOGE in 2025 are certainly impressive--nearly $1 billion in avoided costs represents a significant return on taxpayer investment. However, the initiative's most lasting impact may be cultural rather than fiscal.

"DOGE dumped all of the Medicaid Data and it shows that a Sole Proprietor operating in a van in rural New Mexico has billed $76 MILLION dollars in 7 years...averaging thousands of claims per day...and a Pediatrician who billed Medicaid 830 claims per day..." [@liz_churchill10](https://substack.com/redirect/6d11ae1e-7391-4fbd-9f5c-79a0d01a22f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

DOGE introduced a new mindset across government agencies: that every expenditure must be justified not by tradition or precedent, but by demonstrated value. This philosophical shift has already begun changing how agencies approach procurement, with increased emphasis on:

* Outcome-based contract structures
* Regular performance reviews
* Competition and market research
* Transparency in pricing and decision-making
As we move into 2026, government contractors and federal employees alike are adapting to a new reality shaped by DOGE's 2025 successes. The initiative has proven that thoughtful, data-driven efficiency measures can achieve substantial savings without compromising essential government functions.

Perhaps the most valuable lesson from DOGE's first year is that government efficiency isn't a partisan issue--it's a pragmatic one. By focusing on measurable results rather than political ideology, DOGE has created an approach to government improvement that can withstand changes in administration and continue evolving as new technologies and methodologies emerge.

For American taxpayers, DOGE represents something rare in government: a bold experiment that actually delivered on its promises. In an era of skepticism about federal competence, the 2025 story of DOGE offers a hopeful narrative about what's possible when government commits to doing better with the resources it already has.

The Department of Government Efficiency's transformative impact in 2025 demonstrates a fundamental truth: with the right leadership, tools, and approach, government can indeed become more efficient without sacrificing effectiveness. The nearly $1 billion in savings tells only part of the story--perhaps more significant is the cultural shift toward accountability, performance, and value that DOGE introduced throughout the federal procurement system.

As agencies continue to implement and refine these efficiency initiatives, the savings and improvements will likely compound in the years ahead. For anyone concerned about fiscal responsibility and good governance, DOGE's first year offers a rare piece of genuinely good news from Washington.

Look for our next report on 'The Autism Gold Rush'

"$4.6 million to $85.6 million. One state. One billing code. Four years. Nebraska didn't have an autism epidemic. It had a reimbursement rate that was among the highest in the country and zero accreditation requirements for the companies billing it. Out-of-state operators set up shop. Individual clinicians billing Medicaid grew from 389 to over 2,700. The state had no system to verify whether therapy actually happened. Indiana's federal audit sampled 100 months of ABA claims. Every single one contained at least one improper payment. Not 97. All 100. Nap time billed as treatment. Group therapy billed as individual. Unqualified staff. Missing documentation. This is what a gold rush looks like when the gold is Medicaid money and no one is watching the mine.
